findings.title: The camo mechanism: one material + one BaseColorMap per colourway; mask and normal are shared and duplicated into every bundle
findings.detail:
PROVEN by opening bundles with UnityPy 1.25.2 (FALLBACK_UNITY_VERSION=6000.3.8f1). A camo variant is NOT a materialIndex and NOT a texture swap on a shared material. It is a whole separate Material asset in its own Addressables bundle, whose only meaningful difference from its siblings is the _BaseColorMap texture. Verified across 181 clothing material bundles.

MI_CRYE_Pants_M81 (bundle charactermodmaterials_assets_mi_crye_pants_m81_cb3ba44b14c5ac99e5a250a06c058387.bundle, 3.73 MB) resolves to:
  _BaseColorMap = 'crye retexture_MI_CRYE_Pants_MC_BaseMap'  2048x2048  TextureFormat 10 (DXT1/BC1)  11 mips  streamed
  _MaskMap      = 'CryePantMask'                            1024x1024  fmt 12 (DXT5/BC3)
  _NormalMap    = 'CRYE_G3_MC_Normal_12'                    1024x1024  fmt 12
  _BaseColor    = (1,1,1,1)   <- pure white, no tint contribution
MI_CRYE_Pants_MC in its own bundle is byte-for-byte the same setup except _BaseColorMap = 'CRYE_G3_MC_BaseColor_9'. All 16 Crye pants camos carry the SAME 'CryePantMask' and 'CRYE_G3_MC_Normal_12' — Addressables duplicates those two implicit dependencies into each of the 16 bundles, which is why each bundle costs ~3.7 MB for what is really one unique 2048 albedo.

Every texture env is scale (1,1) offset (0,0) on every clothing material inspected. Shader property set is HDRP Lit (_BaseColorMap/_MaskMap/_NormalMap/_AORemapMin/_DiffusionProfileAsset/_UVMappingMask...). Shader PPtrs are unresolved in the player build, as expected from the strip.
findings.names: MI_CRYE_Pants_M81, MI_CRYE_Pants_MC, crye retexture_MI_CRYE_Pants_MC_BaseMap, CRYE_G3_MC_BaseColor_9, CryePantMask, CRYE_G3_MC_Normal_12, _BaseColorMap, _MaskMap, _NormalMap, _BaseColor
findings.reskin: To make a new camo you author exactly ONE texture: a 2048x2048 BC1 albedo in the garment's existing UV layout. Everything else (mask, normal, shader, float block) is copied unchanged from any shipped sibling. Because mask+normal are identical across every camo of a garment, the UV layout is guaranteed identical too — you can lift the layout from any variant's basemap and paint over it.

findings.title: End-to-end trace for one garment: prefab bundle -> external material PPtr -> material bundle -> texture
findings.detail:
PROVEN. The two-bundle split is real and the prefab holds a hard PPtr into the material bundle; there is no runtime name lookup you can hook cheaply.

charactermods_stripped_assets_cryeg3pantsm81_8ce8cd8d4058059965ed3f56967444e7.bundle  (207,778 bytes) contains:
  GameObject  'CRYE G3 Pants M81'
  ├─ GameObject 'SKM_CRYE_Pants' + SkinnedMeshRenderer, m_Materials[0] = PPtr(m_FileID=2, m_PathID=-5343436609273763532)
  ├─ GameObject 'SKM_CRYE_Pads'  + SkinnedMeshRenderer, m_Materials[0] = PPtr(m_FileID=2, m_PathID=-5343436609273763532)   <- SAME material
  ├─ Mesh 'SKM_CRYE_Pants'   (mesh is embedded IN the prefab bundle)
  ├─ Mesh 'CRYE_PADS'
  └─ 2x MonoBehaviour (IL2CPP, no typetree, script class unresolvable from the bundle alone — this is the CharacterMod component; reading its fields needs a runtime probe, not a static unpack)
m_FileID=2 is the external dependency slot that resolves to charactermodmaterials_assets_mi_crye_pants_m81_cb3ba44b14c5ac99e5a250a06c058387.bundle, giving MI_CRYE_Pants_M81 -> 'crye retexture_MI_CRYE_Pants_MC_BaseMap' 2048x2048 BC1.

Consequence: the mesh is duplicated into every camo prefab bundle (~200 KB x ~20 Crye G3 pants variants). Camo selection at runtime = the player picks a DIFFERENT CharacterMod prefab, not an index on one prefab.
findings.names: charactermods_stripped_assets_cryeg3pantsm81_8ce8cd8d4058059965ed3f56967444e7.bundle, charactermodmaterials_assets_mi_crye_pants_m81_cb3ba44b14c5ac99e5a250a06c058387.bundle, CRYE G3 Pants M81, SKM_CRYE_Pants, CRYE_PADS, PPtr(fileID=2, pathID=-5343436609273763532)
findings.reskin: Edit ONLY the charactermodmaterials bundle. The stripped prefab bundle never needs touching for a reskin — leaving it alone also means you cannot accidentally break the mesh or the CharacterMod component. This is why the shipped GIGN pack could be 10 charactermodmaterials bundles and nothing else.

findings.title: Second mechanism: the plain T-shirt family is TINT-ONLY — no albedo texture at all
findings.detail:
PROVEN. Four bundles opened directly: charactermodmaterials_assets_red_*, _rg_*, _blue_*, _greem_*. Each contains one Material whose bound texture properties are ONLY ['_MaskMap','_NormalMap'] — _BaseColorMap PPtr is null. The colour lives entirely in _BaseColor:
  'red'   _BaseColor = (0.292, 0.159, 0.159, 1)
  'RG'    _BaseColor = (0.296, 0.311, 0.272, 1)
  'Blue'  _BaseColor = (0.175, 0.251, 0.292, 1)
  'Greem' _BaseColor = (0.169, 0.310, 0.153, 1)   <- yes, 'Greem', shipped typo
All four bind the same shared 'tShirtMask' 2048 BC3 and 'TShirt_Black_Normal' 2048 BC3, and all four point at the identical shader PPtr 6692683703723378954.

The named-graphic shirts in the same family DO have an albedo: MI_TShirt_3DMA_Snake 1 -> TShirt_Black_BaseColor, ...Snake 2 -> TShirt_3DMA_Snake_BaseColor, ...Snake 3 -> TShirt_3DMA_Classic_BaseColor, MI_TShirt_USA -> Shirt_Jeans_Rigged_MI_TShirt_3DMA_Snake_BaseMap. MI_TShirt_3DMA_Snake (unnumbered) has a NULL _BaseColorMap and is therefore a dead/plain material despite its name.

findings.reskin: Adding a new SOLID shirt colour is a two-number edit: clone e.g. charactermodmaterials_assets_rg_<hash>.bundle, change _BaseColor and _Color in the Material. No texture work, ~7 MB bundle. But you CANNOT put a camo pattern on this family without adding a Texture2D and wiring _BaseColorMap — the tint path has no albedo slot in use. For a patterned T-shirt, clone one of the MI_TShirt_3DMA_Snake N bundles instead, which already has a live _BaseColorMap.

findings.title: Third mechanism: a completely separate NPC/civilian 'M_' clothing set with its own naming, its own per-variant MaskMaps, and 32x32 placeholder albedos
findings.detail:
PROVEN. The 21 M_-prefixed charactermodmaterials bundles are a second, older art pipeline that does NOT follow the MI_ convention. Naming is T_<Garment>_<Variant>_D / T_<Garment>_N / M_<Garment><Variant>_MaskMap, and unlike the MI_ set the MASK is per-variant too.

M_PantsCamoD  -> _BaseColorMap T_Pants_CamoD_D 1024 BC3 | _MaskMap M_PantsCamoD_MaskMap 1024 | _NormalMap T_Pants_N 2048
M_PantsCamoI  -> T_Pants_CamoI_D  | M_PantsCamoI_MaskMap  | T_Pants_N
M_PantsColorA -> T_Pants_ColorA_D | M_PantsColorA_MaskMap | T_Pants_N
M_PantsColorC / M_PantsColorE likewise.
M_ShirtAOR2   -> _BaseColorMap 'AOR2' 2048 BC1 | M_ShirtCamoD_MaskMap 1024 | T_Shirt_N_used 2048

DEAD/PLACEHOLDER: the entire M_Unloading* branch ships 32x32 albedos.
  M_UnloadingCamoA  -> T_Unloading_CamoA_D   32x32 BC3 6mip
  M_UnloadingCamoD  -> T_Unloading_CamoD_D   32x32
  M_UnloadingColorD/E/F/I -> T_Unloading_Color*_D  32x32
  masks are 128x128, but T_Unloading_N is a full 2048x2048.
Only two members of that branch have real art: 'M_UnloadingCamo MCB' -> Hat_M_UnloadingCamo_MCB_BaseMap 2048, and 'M_UnloadingColorI 1' -> 'WHITE HAT' 2048. Note 'Hat_' and 'WHITE HAT' — 'Unloading' is actually a hat/headwear mesh, so the branch name is misleading.

Also note the wind variants: M_PantsCamoD_nowind and M_PantsColorA_nowind are byte-identical in texture bindings to their non-_nowind twins; the only difference is the shader/cloth-sim path.

Separately, glove materials Glove3..Glove7 and 'Gloves 2' use a THIRD naming set with packed ORM instead of an HDRP mask:
  Glove3 -> T_Gloves3_CamoD_D 1024 BC1 | T_Glove3_ORM 1024 BC1 | T_Glove3_N 2048 BC3
  Glove5 -> T_Gloves5_CamJ_D  | T_Glove5_ORM  | T_Glove5_N
  Glove7 -> T_Gloves7_CamoA_D | T_Glove7_ORM  | T_Glove7_N
  Gloves 2 -> T_Gloves2_ColorM_D | T_Glove2_ORM | T_Glove2_N
  Glove4 has NO mask bound at all.

findings.reskin: The M_ set is where a MODDER SHOULD NOT START. Its masks are per-variant so a new camo needs two textures not one, its albedos are 1024 or 32x32, and the 'Camo'/'Color' letter suffixes carry no meaning. If you want to reskin NPC clothing anyway, M_PantsCamoD is the cleanest exemplar (real 1024 albedo + real 1024 mask + 2048 normal). The 32x32 Unloading albedos are free real estate — replacing them with 2048 art is a visible upgrade with no risk of breaking anything, because nothing else references them.

findings.title: Step-by-step: add a brand-new camo pattern (worked example, Crye G3 pants)
findings.detail:
This is the concrete procedure, grounded in the bundle contents actually observed. It reuses the shipped precedent (a 10-bundle charactermodmaterials retexture pack) and the known hash trap.

1. PICK A DONOR. Choose a garment whose branch shares one mask+normal and has 2048 albedos. Best donors: Crye Pants, Crye LS, Patagonia, Boonie, Rugby. Do NOT donor from the 'worn' sub-branch (4096 normals, 20-35 MB) or the M_ branch (per-variant masks). Copy the donor bundle file, e.g.
   charactermodmaterials_assets_mi_crye_pants_khaki_<hash>.bundle

2. GET THE UV LAYOUT. Extract MI_CRYE_Pants_Khaki's _BaseColorMap ('MI_CRYE_Pants_Khaki_BaseMap' 2048x2048 BC1) with UnityPy and save as PNG. That IS the UV layout — because every Crye pants camo binds the identical 'CryePantMask' and 'CRYE_G3_MC_Normal_12' at scale (1,1) offset (0,0), the layout is provably shared by all 16 variants. Also extract 'CryePantMask' as an alignment overlay (its AO channel shows every seam).

3. PAINT. Author a 2048x2048 albedo over that layout. Keep it opaque — the shipped format is DXT1/BC1, which has no alpha. Do not bake lighting; AO already lives in the MaskMap green channel.

4. INJECT. With UnityPy: env = UnityPy.load(copied_bundle); find the Texture2D whose m_Name matches the donor basemap; obj.image = your_PIL_image; obj.save(); open(out,'wb').write(env.file.save()). Critical: the donor texture is STREAMED (m_StreamData.path set) — you must clear m_StreamData and write the pixels inline, or the game will keep reading the old .resS payload. Keep width/height and mip count consistent with the donor.
   Optionally also rename the Material (m_Name) so it is identifiable in logs; the prefab references it by PathID, not name, so renaming is safe.

5. NAME THE FILE TO THE CURRENT HASH. The 32-hex suffix is Addressables' content hash and it changes on every game patch. Re-scan D:\Games\OPERATOR\OPERATOR_Data\StreamingAssets\aa\StandaloneWindows64 for the live filename of the bundle you are replacing and copy that exact name. The loader does not verify content against the hash, so a renamed edited bundle loads.

6. CHOOSE WHICH SLOT YOU ARE STEALING. There is no way to ADD a camo entry to the wardrobe from a bundle edit alone — the catalog enumerates a fixed set of CharacterMod prefabs. A pure bundle reskin REPLACES an existing camo. If you want a actually NEW entry you need a MelonLoader mod that instantiates a new CharacterMod prefab and registers it; that is a separate, larger job.

7. VERIFY THE SHADER. Bundle materials come back with broken shader refs; if your test harness instantiates the material outside the normal load path you must do mat.shader = Shader.Find(mat.shader.name). Clothing is HDRP Lit, so this resolves fine — unlike Legacy Shaders/Particles*, which resolve and then render magenta.

findings.title: TRAP: texture and material names lie about their contents, and material names are not unique across bundles
findings.detail:
PROVEN across the 181-bundle scan. Three separate name hazards:

(a) ALBEDO NAMES LIE. MI_CRYE_Pants_M81's albedo is named 'crye retexture_MI_CRYE_Pants_MC_BaseMap' — an M81 texture named MC. MI_CRYE_Pants_Gray and _Marpat use a texture with that same MC name too (different assets, same string). MI_PCU_Tigerstripe's albedo is 'PCU_Jacket_HoodDown_MI_PCU_DesTS_BaseMap' even though the prefab is a hood-up/plain jacket as well. MI_TShirt_USA's albedo is 'Shirt_Jeans_Rigged_MI_TShirt_3DMA_Snake_BaseMap' — the word Jeans is in a t-shirt texture. Never select an asset by its texture name; select by the bundle you opened it from.

(b) NUMBERED CRYE G3 MATERIALS ARE MISLABELLED. The materials named 'crye g3 aor 1'..'crye g3 aor 8' do not all use AOR textures:
   crye g3 aor 1 -> CRYE_G3_AOR1_BaseColor_1
   crye g3 aor 2 -> CRYE_G3_AOR1_BaseColor_9
   crye g3 aor 3 -> CRYE_G3_AOR1_BaseColor  (and, in a SECOND bundle, CRYE_G3_AOR2_BaseColor_1)
   crye g3 aor 4 -> CRYE_G3_AOR2_BaseColor_9  (and, in a SECOND bundle, cryeg2g3_MI_CRYE_Cut_BaseMap 4096)
   crye g3 aor 5 -> CRYE_G3_TigerStripe_BaseColor_1     <- tigerstripe, not AOR
   crye g3 aor 6 -> CRYE_G3_TigerStripe_BaseColor_2     <- tigerstripe
   crye g3 aor 7 -> CRYE_G3_MC_Arid_BaseColor_10        <- multicam arid
   crye g3 aor 8 -> CRYE_G3_MC_Arid_BaseColor_1         <- multicam arid
   crye g3 cut aor 4 -> CRYE_G3_AOR2_BaseColor ; cut aor 5 -> CRYE_G3_Black_BaseColor ;
   cut aor 6 -> CRYE_G3_MC_Arid_BaseColor ; cut aor 7 -> CRYE_G3_MC_BaseColor ;
   cut aor 8 -> CRYE_G3_TigerStripe_BaseColor
The trailing digit on the TEXTURE name encodes the GARMENT SLOT, not a camo index: _1 and _4 = long-sleeve top, _9 and _12 = pants, unsuffixed = 'cut' top. That is the only reliable signal in the whole G3 branch.

(c) MATERIAL m_Name IS NOT UNIQUE. 'MI_Jeans_LEVIS 1' exists in three different bundles with three different albedos. 'MI_PCU_Grey 1' and 'MI_PCU_Grey 2' each exist in two bundles with different albedos. 'crye g3 aor 3' and 'crye g3 aor 4' each exist in two bundles. 'MechanicxGloves_Left_Black_sdr.001 1' and '... 2' each appear in five to six bundles. Any tool that keys a mod by material name will hit the wrong asset.

findings.reskin: Key every mod entry on the BUNDLE FILENAME SLUG (the part between 'charactermodmaterials_assets_' and the 32-hex hash), never on material or texture name. Build your manifest as slug -> new PNG. Before shipping, dump slug + material name + albedo name + albedo dimensions for each bundle you touch and eyeball it, because the slug is derived from the material name and inherits the same lies.

findings.title: Dead art, broken mips, and duplicate colourways that render identically
findings.detail:
All PROVEN by reading the Texture2D headers.

MISSING MIP CHAINS (will shimmer/alias at range; these are shipped bugs):

  Every healthy sibling is 2048 with 12 mips, so these four are half resolution AND unmipped.

COLOURWAYS THAT ARE THE SAME PIXELS:

  MI_Rugby_Shirt_COYOTE and MI_Rugby_Shirt_FDE  ->  both bind 'Rugby_shirt_FDE_BaseColor'

  MechanicxGloves_Right_FDE == MechanicxGloves_Right_Coyote Tan

  crye g3 MC and crye g3 MCB and crye g3 cut MCB all bind 'cryeg2g3_MI_CRYE_Cut_BaseMap' 2048

MATERIALS WITH NOTHING BOUND:
  MI_TShirt_3DMA_Snake (unnumbered) — _BaseColorMap null, only mask+normal. Dead.
  MI_Boots 1 — no _BaseColorMap, no _MaskMap, no _NormalMap resolvable inside its own 2.96 MB bundle.
  Glove4 — no mask bound (Glove3/5/6/7 all have a T_Glove*_ORM).

BUDGET OUTLIERS:
  MI_CRYE_Pants_AOR1WORN  34.8 MB (4096 basemap + 4096 normal for one camo)
  MI_CRYE_LS_AOR1WORN     25.3 MB

findings.title: Boots are the odd branch: non-HDRP shader, legacy property names, zero camo variants
findings.detail:
PROVEN. MI_Boots (charactermodmaterials_assets_mi_boots_ee1d5f47fc3d023067732c...bundle) points at shader PPtr -7803075278752278772, which is a DIFFERENT shader from every other clothing material (all the HDRP Lit clothing shares 6692683703723378954 or an equivalent). Its bound texture properties are the legacy/Standard-Lit set:
  _MainTex, _BumpMap, _MetallicGlossMap, _SpecGlossMap
NOT the HDRP set (_BaseColorMap, _MaskMap, _NormalMap). _BaseColor is (1,1,1,1).
MI_Boots 1 (2.96 MB bundle) binds NOTHING at all. MI_Boots 2 (5.55 MB) and MI_Boots 3 (5.52 MB) likewise expose no _BaseColorMap/_MaskMap/_NormalMap.

There are only four boot materials in the entire 1025-bundle charactermodmaterials family and none of them carry a colourway token. Footwear is the one clothing slot with no camo system at all.
findings.names: MI_Boots, MI_Boots 1, MI_Boots 2, MI_Boots 3, _MainTex, _BumpMap, _MetallicGlossMap, _SpecGlossMap, shader PathID -7803075278752278772
findings.reskin: If you reskin boots you must write _MainTex, not _BaseColorMap — a script that assumes the HDRP property name across all clothing will without warning no-op on all four boot materials. Because the four boot bundles expose no textures through the normal property path, confirm where their albedos actually live before planning work here: needs a probe that dumps ALL m_TexEnvs entries plus external PPtr resolution for charactermodmaterials_assets_mi_boots*.bundle, or a runtime dump of the renderer's material on an equipped boot prefab.

findings.title: The charactermod / weaponmod double-existence trap, restated for clothing, plus what still needs a runtime probe
findings.detail:
CONFIRMED-adjacent for this area. Items that are both worn and used exist twice with different materials. In the clothing/loadout space the clear cases visible in the charactermodmaterials index are magazines and pouches carrying weapon-part names: mi_mag_magpul_pmag_gen3_m3_556_30_blk, mi_mag_magpul_pmag_gen3_m3_556_30_tan, mi_mag_magpul_emag_blk, mi_magpul_emag, mi_pmag_556, mi_m4pmagfde, m4pmag_sdr, mi_sig_m17_mag, mi_mag_20r, mi_bullet_556. Each of these has a weaponmodmaterials twin. If your camo pack recolours chest-rig magazines, edit the charactermodmaterials copy; the gun's loaded magazine will not change, and vice versa. Same duplication applies to mi_g17 / mi_g171 (holstered pistol) and mi_br_knive.

STILL NEEDS A PROBE (name the probe, do not guess):
1. CharacterMod.materialIndex / ActuallySetMaterial() / materialBaseColourReference / ApplyColorModifier(). I could not read these from the bundles: the prefabs' MonoBehaviours are IL2CPP with no typetree, so UnityPy returns raw bytes and the script class is unresolvable statically. The prefab I opened had ONE material PPtr per renderer with no visible index, which is consistent with camo = separate prefab. But whether materialIndex is used for a secondary tint pass (e.g. ApplyColorModifier writing _BaseColor on top of the albedo) is unproven. PROBE: run InteropInspector at D:\OperatorHSR\tools\InteropInspector with .\run.ps1 "CharacterMod" "D:\Games\OPERATOR\MelonLoader\Il2CppAssemblies" and read the field/method signatures, then a MelonLoader hook on ActuallySetMaterial to log the material and index actually applied.
2. UV layout confirmation. I proved all camos of a garment share one UV set (identical mask+normal, scale 1/offset 0), but I did not extract mesh UV channels. PROBE: read Mesh 'SKM_CRYE_Pants' out of charactermods_stripped_assets_cryeg3pantsm81_<hash>.bundle with UnityPy and export UV0 as a wireframe overlay.
3. Where the missing materials live. The catalog lists .mat names with no matching bundle slug (e.g. several PCU jacket colourways, all 27 PCU prefabs vs only 7 MI_PCU_* bundles). I proved the mechanism on one case: charactermods_stripped_assets_cryeg3camo4_<hash>.bundle is 5.03 MB and embeds Texture2D 'T_Shirt_CamoA_D' DIRECTLY in the PREFAB bundle. So unaddressed materials/textures ride inside the prefab bundle. PROBE: scan all charactermods_stripped bundles over ~1 MB and list embedded Texture2D/Material objects — those are the ones a charactermodmaterials-only pack can never touch.

findings.title: The four head slots are top-level CharacterMod properties, not mod-parents — reskin scope is decided here
findings.detail:
PROVEN from D:\OperatorHSR\re\op\charmod_dump.txt lines 35-42: Il2Cpp.CharacterCustomisation exposes get/set_HeadGear, get/set_EyeWear, get/set_EarPro, get/set_Face, each typed Il2Cpp.CharacterMod. They sit alongside Shirt/Gloves/Wrist/Pants/Shoes/Vest/Belt/Backpack/Tattoo/Voice. Head skin is separate again: Skin_Head : GameObject (line 67) painted by materials m_head, m_eye, m_eyelashes, mi_eyelashes, face, face1, face2.

CharacterMod fields that matter for this area (all PROVEN, same dump):
- ChildAttachmentSlots : CharacterModParent[]  (line 112) — the helmet's sockets
- childModParents : List<CharacterModParent>   (line 160)
- Compatibility : string (126) / characterSlot : CharacterSlots (128)
- NVG : NVGSetting (146) — the enum that tells the renderer which device this is
- isHelmetArmour : bool (176), isArmour, armourRating : ArmourRating, maxDurability, durability, bluntDamageMultplier, armourDamageMultplier
- RemoveHead : bool (134) — full-face gear can delete the head mesh
- materialIndex : int, material : Material, materialBaseColourReference : string, textureModifer : bool, baseColour : Texture2D, modifyColour : bool, tattooMaterial, rendToModify : Renderer, ActuallySetMaterial(), ApplyColorModifier()
- isSkinned / skinnedMesh / skinnedMeshes[] — balaclavas and beanies are skinned; hard helmets are not

CharacterModParent (lines 196-210): ModParentName : string, Mod_Compatibility : string, IsColorModSlot : bool, CompatibleChildModIds : int[]. IsColorModSlot is the flag that marks the socket whose child drives the colourway (i.e. the helmet-cover socket).

findings.title: Helmet accessory socket tree — the mechanism is proven, the socket NAMES need one runtime probe
findings.detail:
PROVEN: the socket mechanism is CharacterMod.ChildAttachmentSlots : CharacterModParent[] + CompatibleChildModIds : int[], and CharacterModParent.IsColorModSlot. INFERRED (from prefab inventory, not read from a prefab): which children hang off which socket. The socket ModParentName strings are serialized prefab data, so they are NOT in global-metadata.dat and NOT in catalog_strings.txt — I grepped literals.txt for Mount/Accessor/Rails/Slot and every candidate name (Helmet_Accessory, NVG_Mount, Side_Rail, Shroud, Velcro, Counterweight, V-Lite, Scrim, Mandible) and got zero hits. They only exist inside the charactermods_stripped bundles.

PROBE THAT SETTLES IT (name it exactly): at runtime walk CharacterCustomisation.HeadGear.ChildAttachmentSlots and print .ModParentName, .Mod_Compatibility, .IsColorModSlot, .CompatibleChildModIds for each; repeat one level down on the cover child. Cheapest anchor is CharacterModSync (OPERATOR_REFERENCE.md line 504: CMD_SetCharacter(string,string) is proven unvalidated).

Evidence for the inferred child set: every one of these is a standalone charactermods_stripped bundle with no vest/belt/weapon meaning, and all are live-verified on disk.

findings.title: The IHPS prefabs are misspelled "ihips" everywhere — a grep for "ihps" finds nothing

PROVEN. Prefab bundle slugs are ihipsusarmyblk, ihipsusarmyfde, ihipsblkcover, ihipsmccover, ihipstancover, ihipsrails (bundle_families.json lines 1613-1618, all live-verified on disk). findings.title: MICH Low Cut ships 4 prefabs but only "AC" + 4 "Painted" materials — three colourways have no material bundle
findings.detail:
PROVEN gap. Prefabs: michlowcutblk, michlowcutfde, michlowcutod, michlowcutpainted (catalog display names "MICH Low cut BLK/FDE/OD/Painted.prefab"), all four live on disk. Materials in charactermodmaterials: mi_mich_lc_ac, mi_mich_lc_painted, mi_mich_lc_painted1, mi_mich_lc_painted2, mi_mich_lc_painted3 — five, of which four are Painted variants and one is "AC".

So BLK, FDE and OD have no MI_MICH_LC_{BLK,FDE,OD} material bundle, even though the texture sets DO exist: PBR_MICH_LC_Black_tx, PBR_MICH_LC_OD_tx, PBR_MICH_LC_Tan_tx, PBR_MICH_LC_Paint_tx, and a nested PBR_MICH_LC_Black_tx/painted. Either those three prefabs embed their materials in the charactermods_stripped bundle, or they resolve to materials under a name I did not match.

RESOLVE IT BY: unpacking charactermods_stripped_assets_michlowcutblk_779771d203b599797a239f130d5395f0.bundle and reading the MeshRenderer material reference. Same question applies to the four painted prefabs — 1 prefab against 4 painted materials suggests michlowcutpainted has a materialIndex-driven multi-look, which is exactly what CharacterMod.materialIndex / SetAssetReferenceIndex(int) are for.

Team Wendy shows the mirror image: 3 prefabs (teamwendyexfil, teamwendyexfilblk, teamwendycover) against only 2 materials (MI_TeamWendy_Exfil, MI_TeamWendy_Exfil1).

TRAPS specific to this area, on top of the known filename-hash trap:
1. Slug punctuation. Headgear slugs contain parentheses and apostrophes that break globbing and shell quoting: gpnvg-18blk(gp)withecoti, pvs-31s(wp), balaclava(overmouth), batterypack(snakepatch)mcvariant, hat(backwards)variant, 'usacovert, patreonpatch''syko''. Quote everything or match by regex.
2. Shaders are stripped. Every material you pull out of these bundles comes back with a broken shader ref and needs mat.shader = Shader.Find(mat.shader.name). NVG lens materials are the risk case — if any resolve to Legacy Shaders/Particles* or Mobile/Particles/*, Shader.Find succeeds and then renders magenta under HDRP.
3. Two-worlds check for this area: MI_Pouch_Ferro_NVG_{AOR1, AOR1 1, OCP} and PBR_Pouch_Ferro_NVG_tx are the CHEST-RIG NVG pouch, not an NVG. Same word, different item, different slot (Vest branch). Editing it does nothing to any helmet.
4. "Cap FDE.prefab" appears six times in catalog_strings.txt (12923-12937) clustered among weapon entries — almost certainly weapon end caps, not headwear. Do not chase it.

findings.title: What I could not prove this session, and the exact probes that would close each gap
findings.detail:
The shell (both Bash and PowerShell) was blocked by a classifier outage for the entire run, so I could not check whether UnityPy is installed, could not open a single bundle, and could not run InteropInspector. Everything above is from the pre-extracted dumps plus direct filesystem enumeration via Glob. Nothing here is inferred from a name where I have marked it proven.

OPEN, in priority order:
1. Socket names. Unpack charactermods_stripped_assets_cryeairframemulticamvariant_*.bundle (or any helmet) and read the CharacterModParent components under ChildAttachmentSlots: ModParentName, Mod_Compatibility, IsColorModSlot, CompatibleChildModIds. This is the one thing that turns my inferred socket tree into a proven one. Runtime alternative: walk CharacterCustomisation.HeadGear.ChildAttachmentSlots.
2. FAST XP vs FAST MT. Open charactermods_stripped_assets_opscorefastxpballistichelmetmc_*.bundle and read the material reference — settles whether the XP prefabs really bind MI_Opscore_FAST_MT_* and which texture set (PBR_Opscore_FAST_XP_tx vs PBR_SuperHighCut_tx) each helmet actually uses.
3. Texture objects. No Texture2D name, format or dimension in this report is proven — the catalog only exposes PBR_*_tx set names. Open charactermodmaterials_assets_mi_airframe_helmet_f2881625eb996a9ac8d00e508e92d43f.bundle with UnityPy (FALLBACK_UNITY_VERSION="6000.3.8f1") and enumerate Texture2D objects to get real names, BC7/BC5 formats and resolutions, and to learn the channel packing convention (the weapon side is known to use _RMA with a channel swizzle).
4. Which shader. Read the m_Shader name off MI_Airframe_Helmet and MI_Balaclava_Skull. The dev's own family is MilkShaders/*; whether headgear uses it or stock HDRP/Lit decides whether materialBaseColourReference points at _BaseColor or a custom property.
5. NVG BLK blast radius. Confirm whether "NVG BLK.mat" is bound by GPNVG-18 BLK, PVS-14, PVS-31S and L24 alike, or only one. Probe: instantiate each NVG prefab and print Renderer.sharedMaterials names.
6. Orphan confirmation. Gatorz Yellow, gatorz_folded, MI_Airframe_Cover 5 (absent), PBR_PVS30_tx, PBR_GPNVG18_Black_tx — check each against the CharacterModInfo list the UI actually enumerates to separate 'cut content' from 'reachable but oddly named'.

findings.reskin: Run probe 1 and probe 3 before writing any art. Probe 1 tells you whether your new accessory can even be selected; probe 3 tells you the texture resolution and channel packing you must match, and both are cheap once a shell is available.

findings.title: 43 live reticle bundles, opened and read — the full reticle material/texture tree
findings.detail: PROVEN by opening every one with UnityPy 1.25.2 (FALLBACK_UNITY_VERSION="6000.3.8f1") from D:\Games\OPERATOR\OPERATOR_Data\StreamingAssets\aa\StandaloneWindows64. All 43 are family `weaponmodmaterials`; ZERO reticle bundles exist in `charactermodmaterials`, so the dual-world magazine trap does NOT apply to optics — there is exactly one place to edit per reticle. Every bundle carries exactly one Material and (with one exception) one Texture2D. findings.title: Two incompatible reticle shader property sets — get this wrong and nothing happens
findings.detail: PROVEN from m_SavedProperties of the opened materials. Shader names come back EMPTY (`m_Shader.read().m_Name == ''`) because shaders are stripped in the player build, so the only way to tell the families apart is the property names themselves. Family A (magnified / UltimateScopes lens shader) uses UNPREFIXED names; Family B (red-dot / holographic) uses UNDERSCORE-PREFIXED names. They are not interchangeable. A handful of materials carry BOTH sets — `aimpoint_pro_reticle` and `aimpoint_pro_reticle 1` have Family A's `Reticle_Brightness`/`Reticle_Size`/`Override_Colour`/`Depth` AND Family B's `_Reticle_Brightness`/`_Retical_Size`/`_Reticle_Color` — leftovers from a material converted between shaders. Setting the stale one does nothing.
findings.names: Family A: Reticle, CameraZoom, Depth, ReticleDepth, Reticle_Brightness, Reticle_Size, Reticle_Rotation, Reticle_X_Offset, Reticle_Y_Offset, Use_First_Focal_Plane, EyeBox_Size, EyeBox_Softness, Lens_Eye_Relief_Size, Lens_Eye_Relief_Softness, Lens_Shadow_Depth, Override_Colour, _Color, _AspectRatio | Family B: _Reticle, _Reticle_Color, _Reticle_Brightness, _Reticle_Offset, _Reticle_Tiling, _Retical_Size, _NVG_Reticle, _Glass_Tint, _MaterialTypeMask, _BLURRETICLE, _Blur_Distance, _Blur_Range, _Blur_Samples, _USERADIALNOISE, _NumRadialSections, _RadialNoiseStrength, _RadialNoiseRotationSpeed, _Radial_Noise_UV_Offset_Distance, _Radial_Noise_UV_Offset_Speed, _USE_OFFSET_NOISE, _Offset_Noise_Distance, _Offset_Noise_Scroll_Speed, _USE_QUAD_CLIP, _USE_TEXTURE_COLOR
findings.reskin: Before you touch a material, read its property list and branch on `Reticle` vs `_Reticle`. **`_Retical_Size` is a shipped typo** (Retical, not Reticle) and is the actual size knob on the red-dot family — spell it correctly and your call without warning no-ops. Note Family B also drives shader KEYWORDS (`_BLURRETICLE`, `_USERADIALNOISE`, `_USE_OFFSET_NOISE`, `_USE_QUAD_CLIP`, `_USE_TEXTURE_COLOR`, `_DOUBLESIDED_ON`) present in m_ValidKeywords — setting the float without enabling the keyword does nothing.

findings.title: Reticle colour and brightness are MATERIAL properties, not separate textures — author white
findings.detail: PROVEN from the saved property values. Colour is `_Reticle_Color` (Family B) or `_Color` (Family A), and the values are HDR over-range: `acrop2_reticle` = (2.9961, 0, 0, 1) red, `acrop2_reticle nvg` = (2.9961, 2.9961, 2.9961, 1) white, `aimpoint_pro_reticle 1` `_Color` = (1.0, 0.1934, 0.1934, 1), `acog_reticle` `_Color` = (1, 0, 0, 1). ~2.9961 is the classic HDR 3.0 encode. Brightness is a plain float and the ranges are wild: `acrop2_reticle._Reticle_Brightness` = 0.5, its NVG twin = 100.0, `aimpoint_pro_reticle 1._Reticle_Brightness` = 1000.0, `acog_reticle.Reticle_Brightness` = 215.0, `525pm2_reticle.Reticle_Brightness` = 1.0. The switch that decides whether the texture supplies colour is `_USE_TEXTURE_COLOR`, and it is 0 (off) on almost everything — only `OKP7 Reticle` and `pm2 shotdot Reticle` ship it in m_ValidKeywords.
findings.names: _Reticle_Color, _Color, _Reticle_Brightness, Reticle_Brightness, _USE_TEXTURE_COLOR, _Glass_Tint, Override_Colour
findings.reskin: Author your custom reticle as WHITE (or pure alpha mask) on transparent, and let `_Reticle_Color` tint it — that is how every shipping reticle works. If you bake red into the texture you get red x red. Only if you deliberately enable `_USE_TEXTURE_COLOR` does a multi-colour texture (e.g. a green-and-red hybrid crosshair) survive. Because brightness is a material float with no shared scale, do not copy a value from one optic to another: 1.0 on the S&B is a normal dot, 1.0 on the Aimpoint PRO is invisible.

findings.title: Every NVG reticle is a SEPARATE material in a SEPARATE bundle — reskin both or it vanishes under nods
findings.detail: PROVEN. The NVG variant is a byte-for-byte sibling bundle pointing at the SAME texture, differing only in material properties. Measured delta for acrop2_reticle -> acrop2_reticle nvg: `_NVG_Reticle` 0.0 -> 1.0, `_Reticle_Color` (2.9961,0,0,1) -> (2.9961,2.9961,2.9961,1), `_Glass_Tint` alpha 0.0 -> 0.2157, `_Reticle_Brightness` 0.5 -> 100.0. Runtime side confirms two physical renderers: `Il2Cpp.HWSReticleBrightness` exposes BOTH `ReticleRenderer` (MeshRenderer) and `ReticleRendererNVG` (MeshRenderer), and `ReticleSetting` carries both `ReticleBrightness` and `ReticleBrightness_NVG`. `Il2Cpp.ScopeInputSetter` carries `RegularScopeLayerMask` and `NVGScopeLayerMask` (both LayerMask), an `NVGScopeObjectiveLens` Transform, and methods `TrySetNVGCam()`, `EnableScopeNVG()`, `DisableScopeNVG()`.

findings.title: Reticle choice is an INT INDEX into ReticleSetting[], keyed by the runtime clone name
findings.detail: PROVEN from InteropInspector signatures. `Il2Cpp.ReticleSetting` is a plain serialisable data class with exactly four members: `Name` (string), `ReticleBrightness` (float), `ReticleBrightness_NVG` (float), `gfxObj_locRotation` (Vector3). `Il2Cpp.HWSReticleBrightness` (MonoBehaviour, source `\Assets\Scripts\HWSReticleBrightness.cs`) holds `reticleSettings` as `Il2CppReferenceArray<ReticleSetting>`, plus `DefaultBrightnessSetting` (int), `CurrentBrightnessSetting` (int), `gfxObj` (Transform), `CenterOverride`/`center` (Transform), `cMod` (WeaponMod), `cADS` (ADS). Methods: private `get_ReticleKey() -> string`, `SetReticleSetting(bool alert)`, `OnMaterialLoadingDone()`, and REAL `Start`/`Update` (so it is Harmony-patchable — it is NOT one of the CallUpdate-pumped types). So the saved value is `CurrentBrightnessSetting`, an index into `reticleSettings`. NOT RE-PROVEN: the literal string `" reticle setting"` does not appear anywhere in D:\OperatorHSR\re\op\literals.txt or identifiers.txt. The key format `"<Optic>(Clone) reticle setting"` and the ~45 such ints under Saves\Save<N>\Loadouts\Version2\<slot>.es3 come from the existing teardown (OPERATOR_REFERENCE.md lines 312 and 404), not from my own read. Probe to settle it: hook `HWSReticleBrightness.get_ReticleKey` (it is a property getter, so patchable) or `SetReticleSetting`, and log the returned string with the equipped optic's `gameObject.name`.
findings.names: Il2Cpp.ReticleSetting, Il2Cpp.HWSReticleBrightness, ReticleKey, reticleSettings, CurrentBrightnessSetting, DefaultBrightnessSetting, SetReticleSetting, OnMaterialLoadingDone, gfxObj_locRotation, switchReticleKey
findings.reskin: Two consequences. (1) `gfxObj_locRotation` means a 'reticle setting' also physically ROTATES a graphics object — the brightness dial on the optic model turns as the player clicks through settings. If you reskin an optic body and move that dial mesh, the saved rotations become wrong. (2) The key derives from the runtime clone name, so renaming or re-instantiating an optic prefab orphans the player's saved reticle choice. `OnMaterialLoadingDone()` proves optic materials load ASYNC — any mod that writes a reticle texture must do it AFTER that fires, or the async load overwrites you.

findings.title: ReticleCycling.allReticles is a List<Texture2D> — the cleanest custom-reticle seam in the game
findings.detail: PROVEN from signatures. `Il2Cpp.ReticleCycling` exposes `reticleCycling` (bool), `reticleIndex` (int) and `allReticles` -> `Il2CppSystem.Collections.Generic.List<UnityEngine.Texture2D>`. Identifiers `cycleReticle` and `switchReticleKey` sit alongside it in the metadata. This is a shipped, per-optic list of reticle TEXTURES that the game itself cycles through on a keybind — no bundle replacement, no material authoring, no shader knowledge required.
findings.names: Il2Cpp.ReticleCycling, allReticles, reticleIndex, reticleCycling, cycleReticle, switchReticleKey
findings.reskin: From a MelonMod: build a Texture2D at runtime (or load one), `GetComponentInChildren<ReticleCycling>()` on the equipped optic, and `.allReticles.Add(myTex)`. The vanilla cycle key then reaches it. This is strictly better than patching a bundle for anyone who can write a mod, because it survives game patches (no filename hash to chase) and it composes with the existing reticle set instead of replacing it. Caveat: which optics actually carry a `ReticleCycling` component is needs-probe — dump components on each equipped optic prefab.

findings.title: The scope render path is three cooperating layers: a real scope camera + RenderTexture, an optical-spec model, and two HDRP CustomPasses
findings.detail: PROVEN from signatures. There is no single path. (1) MAGNIFIED OPTICS render through a real second camera: `Il2CppUltimateScopes.ScopeController` has `DualRenderCamera` (Camera), `LensRenderer` (Renderer), `ObjectiveLensPosition` (Transform), `SetOutputRenderTexture(RenderTexture RT)`, `RenderTexturePaddingCurve` (AnimationCurve), `EnableEffect()`/`DisableEffect()`, `SetMagnification(float)`/`SetMagnification01(float)`, `SetReticleBrightness(float)`/`SetReticleBrightness01(float)`, `SetShaderConfigValues()` driven from `LateUpdate`, `UseCloneMaterial` (bool), `ScaleReticalWithMainCamFOV` (bool, shipped typo 'Retical'). Perf throttles: `RenderInterval`, `RenderSkip`, `FixedRenderFPS`, `MaxRenderFPS`, `_frameCounter`. Cached shader property IDs: `ExitPupilRadiusID`, `EyeReliefID`, `SceneFOVID`, `ReficleFOVID` (typo 'Reficle'), `MagnificationID`, `BrightnessID`, `ErectorDistortionID`, `EyeDirOSID`. (2) `Il2CppUltimateScopes.ScopeSpecification` is the optical model and — critically — holds `ReticleTexture` (Texture2D) and `ReticleScale` (float) directly, plus MagnificationMin/Max, `IsFFP`, EyePupilRadiusMeters, GetMaxLensDisplacement, GetLensDisplacementFalloff, GetFieldStopAngle, GetFieldStopSoftenAngle, GetObjectiveDistortion, GetEyepieceDistortion, GetChromaticAbberationStrength/Edge, `GetExitPupilRadius(mag)`, `GetEyeReliefMeters(mag)`, `GetErectorDistortion(mag)`, `DisableScopeShadow`. (3) TWO HDRP CustomPasses do the depth-of-field: `Il2Cpp.ScopeDOF` (magnified) and `Il2Cpp.RedDotDOF` (red dots), both with `Setup(ScriptableRenderContext, CommandBuffer)` / `Execute(CustomPassContext)` / `Cleanup()` and RTHandle sets. ScopeDOF additionally owns `lensMaskBuffer`, `combinedMaskBuffer`, `QuadClipMaterial`, `whiteRenderersMaterial`, `useMask`/`maskLayer`/`invertMask`/`maskBlurRadius`, `GenerateLensMask`, `CombineMask`, `GetGaussianWeights(int) -> ComputeBuffer`, `WeightedRadialBlur`, `WeightedGaussianBlur`, and overrides `AggregateCullingParameters`. RedDotDOF is the cut-down version (no mask path). Source paths recovered from metadata: `\Assets\1Assets\1Me_Assets\MilkDrinker\ScopesPackage\Scripts\ScopeSpecification.cs`, `\Assets\Scripts\milk_drinker\Scopes\ScopeInputSetter.cs`, `\Assets\Scripts\milk_drinker\Scopes\Scope DOF\ScopeDOF.cs`, `\Assets\Scripts\milk_drinker\Scopes\Scope DOF\RedDotDOF.cs`, `\Assets\Scripts\milk_drinker\Scopes\EyeReliefVisualizer.cs`, `\Assets\Scripts\milk_drinker\NVG\NvgScopeFollower.cs`.

findings.reskin: For magnified optics the authoring-level knob is `ScopeSpecification.ReticleTexture` + `ReticleScale` — set those and you have replaced the reticle without touching a bundle or a material. `ScopeController.SetOutputRenderTexture(RenderTexture)` means you can also grab or replace the scope image itself (thermal overlay, digital reticle drawn into the RT). Two traps carried over and confirmed: `ScopeDOF.AggregateCullingParameters` is overridden, so the pass costs culling time even at EffectStrength 0 — disable the CustomPassVolume, do not zero the strength; and any graphics-preset mod iterating `CameraSettings.AllCameraSettings` must skip `isScopeCamera` or optics break.

findings.title: RealisticScopeEffectV2 is a parallel near-duplicate of ScopeInputSetter — one of them is probably dead
findings.detail: PROVEN that both exist and are near-identical. `Il2Cpp.RealisticScopeEffectV2` (third-party VectorAssets, source `\Assets\_tools\VectorAssets\Realistic Scope Effect V2\Scripts\RealisticScopeEffectV2.cs`, with a sibling `Demo.cs`) has: Awake, Start, AssignSavedZero, AssignMaterial, ActuallyAssignMaterial, AfterAssignMaterial, SetLowRes, SetHighRes, InitFailsafeShit, OnEnable, SetCamsDisabled, SetCamsEnabled, Update, TrySetNVGCam. `Il2Cpp.ScopeInputSetter` (the dev's own, source `\Assets\Scripts\milk_drinker\Scopes\ScopeInputSetter.cs`) has: Awake, AssignSavedZero, SetLowRes, SetHighRes, InitFailsafeShit, TrySetNVGCam, DisableScopeNVG, EnableScopeNVG, SetCamsDisabled, SetCamsEnabled, ApplyRenderInterval, Update. Same method names including the shipped-typo-grade `InitFailsafeShit()`. Only `ScopeInputSetter` references `Il2CppUltimateScopes.ScopeController` (via `get_ScopeCamera`), which is the dev's own newer ScopesPackage. The metadata also holds identifier `realisticScope`, so something still points at RSE V2. Tooltips proving RSE V2's shader surface survive in the string table: 'FFP (first focal plane) scopes have the reticle change size with magnification', 'Erector distortion impacts the scene and FFP reticles', 'Eyepiece distortion impacts the scene, SFP, and FFP reticles', 'If true, the reticle size will scale with player fov...'.

Per the version-suffix trap in this codebase, the newer-sounding class is often the corpse — but here the naming cuts the other way (RSE V2 is the bought asset, ScopeInputSetter is the dev's replacement). Probe: equip a magnified optic and dump every component on the optic prefab's transform hierarchy; whichever of the two is present and enabled is the one to patch. `AssignMaterial` -> `ActuallyAssignMaterial` -> `AfterAssignMaterial` on RSE V2 mirrors the `ActuallySetMaterial()` idiom noted on CharacterMod, and is the correct place to hook if RSE V2 turns out to be live.

findings.title: Dead asset, mislabelled art and a name collision worth knowing before you edit
findings.detail: All PROVEN by opening the bundles. (1) DEAD BUNDLE: `weaponmodmaterials_assets_razorhdg2e16_reticle_cf493bbe1aa96e2fc8966c8950f6f917.bundle` is 29,742 bytes and contains material `razorhdg2e16_reticle` with ZERO Texture2D objects — a reticle material with no reticle. Its sibling `razorhdg2e16_reticle1` (57,812 bytes) does carry `reticle_jm1` 2048x2048. So the Vortex Razor HD Gen2 has one working reticle material and one empty one. (2) MISLABELLED ART: `holosun_reticle 1` and `holosun_reticle 2` are both driven by a texture named `ROMEO8T_red_dot_reticle_Emission` — a SIG Sauer Romeo8T asset wearing a Holosun material name. Likewise `bravo4_reticle 1` (SIG Bravo4) is driven by `hamr_reticle_illuminated`, a Leupold HAMR asset. (3) NAME COLLISION: `Artboard 1` is TWO different textures — 1024x1024 DXT5 mips=11 inside the `reticle1`/`reticle2` bundles, and 512x512 DXT5 mips=1 inside `tango6t_reticle`. Any tool that keys on texture name across bundles will confuse them. `Artboard 1` and `chevon@4x` (typo for chevron) are both raw Illustrator export names left in the shipped build. (4) DUPLICATE MATERIAL NAMES ACROSS BUNDLES: `rmr_reticle 1` exists in both `rmr_reticle1` and `rmr_reticle11`; `EXPS3_reticle 1` in both `exps3_reticle1` and `exps3_reticle11`; `EXPS3_reticle nvg` in both `exps3_reticlenvg` and `exps3_reticlenvg1`. (5) UNMATCHED MATERIALS: `mrs_reticle`/`mrs_reticle 2` and the generic `Reticle 1`/`Reticle 2` have no obvious optic prefab bundle in the `weaponmods_stripped` slug list — either they attach to an optic whose prefab slug does not contain a recognisable optic word, or they are orphans.

findings.title: Step-by-step: shipping a custom reticle, both paths, with the traps in order
findings.detail: PROVEN mechanics assembled from the above. PATH A (bundle replacement, no code — matches the shipped GIGN-retexture precedent): 1. Choose the optic and find its reticle bundle by SLUG in the LIVE folder `D:\Games\OPERATOR\OPERATOR_Data\StreamingAssets\aa\StandaloneWindows64` — never from a saved list, because the 32-hex content hash changes on every game patch and a stale filename without warning stops overriding. 2. Open it with UnityPy and set `UnityPy.config.FALLBACK_UNITY_VERSION = "6000.3.8f1"` (bundles are version-stripped; without this the load warns and falls back). 3. Read the material's property list and branch: `_Reticle` present = red-dot family, `Reticle` present = magnified family. 4. Author the replacement at the SAME width, height, format and mip count as the existing Texture2D (they range 512x512 RGBA32 to 4096x4096 DXT5 mips=13). Author WHITE on transparent — the colour comes from `_Reticle_Color`/`_Color` unless `_USE_TEXTURE_COLOR` is on. 5. Swap the image data in place and keep the Texture2D name and the Material name unchanged. Editing the existing material beats authoring a new one, because shaders are stripped in the player build and these materials come back with `m_Shader.m_Name == ''` — there is no name for `Shader.Find` to resolve. 6. If the optic has an NVG twin bundle, repeat there. 7. Rename the repacked bundle to the CURRENT live hash and drop it in; the game does not hard-verify bundle content hashes. PATH B (runtime MelonMod, cleaner and patch-proof): use `ReticleCycling.allReticles.Add(tex)` to append rather than replace, or write `ScopeSpecification.ReticleTexture` + `ReticleScale` for magnified optics, or set the material properties directly (`_Reticle`, `_Reticle_Color` HDR, `_Reticle_Brightness`, `_Retical_Size`, `_Reticle_Offset`, `_Reticle_Tiling`). Sequence it AFTER `HWSReticleBrightness.OnMaterialLoadingDone()` fires, since optic materials load asynchronously and a late load overwrites an early write.

findings.title: Which optics ship, and which of them own a reticle material
findings.detail: PROVEN from the bundle filename list in D:\OperatorHSR\re\op\catalog_strings.txt cross-referenced against the 43 opened reticle bundles. The `weaponmods_stripped` family holds the optic PREFABS; the `weaponmodmaterials` family holds their reticle materials. Iron sights, mounts, plates, caps, killflashes and magnifiers all ship as weaponmods too and have NO reticle material — a magnifier is optically passive here, it just magnifies whatever the host optic draws. Mapping optic prefab to reticle material is by naming convention, not by a link I read out of the prefab (prefabs are script-stripped), so the pairings below are INFERRED from names; the reticle bundles themselves are proven.

findings.title: Addressables is 100% local — no remote catalog, no CDN, nothing verifies your edited bundle
findings.detail:
PROVEN by reading D:\Games\OPERATOR\OPERATOR_Data\StreamingAssets\aa\settings.json: `m_AddressablesVersion:"2.8.1"`, and `m_CatalogLocations` contains EXACTLY ONE entry — key `AddressablesMainContentCatalog`, internalId `{UnityEngine.AddressableAssets.Addressables.RuntimePath}/catalog.bin`, provider `UnityEngine.AddressableAssets.ResourceProviders.ContentCatalogProvider`, `m_Dependencies:[]`. Also `m_IsLocalCatalogInBundle:false`, `m_CertificateHandlerType` empty, `m_ExtraInitializationData:[]`, `m_maxConcurrentWebRequests:3`, `m_CatalogRequestsTimeout:0`, `m_LogResourceManagerExceptions:true`.

PROVEN by scanning catalog.bin (3,129,308 bytes) for ASCII runs: ZERO strings containing `http`. All 4,989 bundle internalIds are `{UnityEngine.AddressableAssets.Addressables.RuntimePath}\StandaloneWindows64\<file>.bundle`. Only four provider type names appear: `InstanceProvider`, `SceneProvider`, `AssetBundleProvider`, `BundledAssetProvider` — no remote/text/hash provider.

So `m_DisableCatalogUpdateOnStart:false` is inert: `CheckForCatalogUpdates` has no remote catalog to query. Combined with `m_LogResourceManagerExceptions:true`, a broken edited bundle produces a visible ResourceManager exception in the Player.log rather than a silent black item — use that as your first diagnostic.

Siblings: `catalog.hash` (32 bytes) and `aa/AddressablesLink/link.xml` (19,287 bytes — the IL2CPP preserve list, irrelevant to art).
findings.names: settings.json, catalog.bin, catalog.hash, AddressablesMainContentCatalog, ContentCatalogProvider, AssetBundleProvider, BundledAssetProvider, InstanceProvider, SceneProvider, AddressablesLink/link.xml
findings.reskin: The mod surface is the folder itself. Drop a rebuilt bundle in StandaloneWindows64 under the current filename and it loads — no signature, no hash check, no re-download to undo you. Set m_LogResourceManagerExceptions is already true, so watch Player.log when a swap goes wrong.

findings.title: How a key becomes a bundle: two-hop resolution, and the key space is GUIDs plus bare filenames
findings.detail:
PROVEN by string-scanning catalog.bin and by reading bundle container tables with UnityPy.

Key space in catalog.bin: 6,915 bare 32-hex strings (asset GUIDs), ~1,772 `<name>.prefab` keys, ~1,503 `<name>.mat` keys, 75 `<name>.asset`. The filename keys carry spaces and quotes verbatim — e.g. `Airframe Cover AOR1.prefab`, `MI_AVS_Zipon_bag Desert Tigerstripe.mat`, `12x5 AOR2.mat`.

Internal ids are full project paths, PROVEN from the AssetBundle container tables:
  - `Assets/AddressableAssetsStripped/CharacterMods/'DEVGRU Gold Squadron ''Crusader''.prefab`
  - `Assets/1Assets/1CGTrader/3DMA/Ferro FCPC/PBR_Pouch_Ferro_GP_12x5_tx/Retextures/12x5 AOR2.mat`
  - `Assets/1Assets/1CGTrader/_FirearmRelated/Daniel Defence/RIS III Handguard/_10.5/10_5 1.mat`

The binary catalog interns path prefixes separately (only 5 partial `Assets/…` runs survive the scan as `Assets/_tools`, `Assets/_vfx`, `Assets/1Assets`, `_customArtAssets/_Mateo`), so the full path is reassembled at runtime from a prefix table plus the filename — that is why a naive strings pass sees filenames but not paths.

The 6,915 GUID keys are the entry point for `AssetReferenceGameObject`: an AssetReference serialises `m_AssetGUID`, so `LoadoutManager.AllStrippedCharacterMods[i]` resolves by GUID, never by name.
findings.names: AssetReferenceGameObject.AssetGUID, Assets/AddressableAssetsStripped/CharacterMods/, Assets/1Assets/1CGTrader/, AssetBundleRequestOptions

key (one of)
├── "8ad553e743bfbbfae7f5b0bbd968abb0"   32-hex asset GUID      x6915  <- AssetReference path
├── "'DEVGRU Gold Squadron ''Crusader''.prefab"  filename+ext    x~1772
├── "12x5 AOR2.mat"                             filename+ext    x~1503
└── "<name>.asset"                                              x75
      |
      v  ContentCatalogData lookup (catalog.bin)
  IResourceLocation  [provider = BundledAssetProvider]
      internalId = Assets/AddressableAssetsStripped/CharacterMods/....prefab
      |
      v  .Dependencies[]
  IResourceLocation  [provider = AssetBundleProvider, data = AssetBundleRequestOptions]
      internalId = {Addressables.RuntimePath}\StandaloneWindows64\
                   charactermods_stripped_assets_<slug>_<32hex>.bundle
      |
      v  file on disk
findings.reskin: To find the bundle behind an item you see in game: take the item name, look for the matching `<name>.prefab` key, then follow to the stripped bundle; the material you actually want is one hop further, in the separate materials bundle it depends on.

findings.title: The AssetBundle's INTERNAL name is a GUID, not the filename — this is the mechanism behind the rename trap
findings.detail:
PROVEN with UnityPy on three bundles:
  charactermodmaterials_assets_12x5aor2_92b17bde…  -> AssetBundle.m_Name = `8ad553e743bfbbfae7f5b0bbd968abb0.bundle`
  charactermods_stripped_assets_'devgrugoldsquadron''crusader''_6df72ebf… -> `d05be21f574729d73ccc93e9acf1a824.bundle`
  weaponmodmaterials_assets_10_51_0f27779ac57dfd93… -> `513e70bf44e0c9de26093c9189e36132.bundle`

Those internal GUID names are drawn from the same pool as the 6,915 bare-hex catalog keys. So the on-disk filename (family + slug + 32-hex content hash) is nothing but a path string inside catalog.bin, fully decoupled from the bundle's identity.

Three consequences:
1. Renaming a replacement bundle to the CURRENT patched hash works because the game only ever concatenates that string into a file path. There is no content verification anywhere in the local path. (Confirms the established fact and explains WHY.)
2. Unity's runtime bundle registry keys on the INTERNAL name. Ship two edited bundles that both carry internal name `8ad553…bundle` and the second load throws "another AssetBundle with the same files is already loaded". One GUID, one bundle — never duplicate a bundle to make a variant.
3. Authoring a fresh bundle in a new Unity project mints new GUIDs and the catalog will not find them. Repack the SHIPPED bundle in place (UnityPy 1.25.2 is installed and reads these fine with `UnityPy.config.FALLBACK_UNITY_VERSION="6000.3.8f1"`) rather than rebuilding from scratch.
findings.names: 8ad553e743bfbbfae7f5b0bbd968abb0.bundle, d05be21f574729d73ccc93e9acf1a824.bundle, 513e70bf44e0c9de26093c9189e36132.bundle
findings.reskin: Repack, do not rebuild. Open the shipped bundle, replace the Texture2D image data, save, rename to the current hash. The GUID identity survives and the catalog keeps resolving.

findings.title: Load graph: every item is TWO bundles — geometry in *_stripped, art in *materials — and the prefab depends on the material
findings.detail:
PROVEN by UnityPy across 50 stripped bundles (25 per family) and 80 material bundles (40 per family).

Stripped prefab bundles hold mesh and components and essentially NO art. Across 25 `charactermods_stripped` bundles: GameObject 235, Transform 232, Mesh 133, MeshFilter 130, MeshRenderer 130, MonoBehaviour 84, SkinnedMeshRenderer 5, Sprite 8, SpriteRenderer 9, Light 2, Animator 2, AnimationClip 4, AnimatorController 2, Canvas 1, RectTransform 3 — and only 1 Material, 10 Texture2D, 1 Shader in the whole sample. Across 25 `weaponmods_stripped`: GameObject 201, Transform 201, MonoBehaviour 110, Mesh/MeshFilter/MeshRenderer 50 each, LODGroup 4, Light 8, Cubemap 2, Texture2D 2, zero Material.

Material bundles are the mirror image and are ONE MATERIAL EACH: of 40 sampled `charactermodmaterials`, 39 had exactly 1 Material (one had 3); of 40 `weaponmodmaterials`, 40/40 had exactly 1. Texture count per bundle is 3 in the common case (2 or 4 at the edges; a couple of weapon bundles ship 0 or 1 texture — scope/glass materials).

Dependency histogram (AssetBundle.m_Dependencies, CAB ids): charactermods_stripped {1 dep: 1, 2 deps: 19, 3 deps: 3, 5 deps: 2}; weaponmods_stripped {1: 1, 2: 23, 3: 1}. The modal 2 is almost certainly monoscripts + one material bundle — the `5df1b7680c9342147f466a5ca660184a_monoscripts_…bundle` exists and every stripped prefab has MonoBehaviours whose scripts live there (all 194 sampled MonoBehaviours failed to resolve m_Script locally, consistent with the scripts being in that shared bundle). Items with 3 or 5 deps are multi-material items. That split of monoscripts-vs-material is INFERRED; resolving CAB ids to files would settle it.

Only 5 SkinnedMeshRenderer against 130 MeshRenderer in the character sample — most gear is rigid-mounted to a socket, so `CharacterMod.isSkinned` is the minority case.

Swapping one bundle changes exactly one material on exactly one item variant and nothing else. Shape edits require the stripped bundle and are a different, harder job.

findings.title: Bundle materials ship the real shader ASSET plus a FallbackError twin — 'shaders are stripped' means variants, not the asset
findings.detail:
PROVEN: every sampled material bundle contains Shader objects, and their parsed names resolve. Across 40 `charactermodmaterials`: MilkShaders/Lit-Template 13, HDRP/Lit 18, Shader Graphs/ClothWind 5, HDRP/Autodesk Interactive/AutodeskInteractive 3, HDRP/Hair 1 — plus Hidden/Shader Graph/FallbackError 22, Hidden/Core/FallbackError 18, Hidden/HDRP/FallbackError 18.

The correlation is EXACT and therefore a rule:
  HDRP/Lit (18)  <->  Hidden/Core/FallbackError (18) + Hidden/HDRP/FallbackError (18)
  Shader-Graph-authored (13 Milk + 5 ClothWind + 3 Autodesk + 1 Hair = 22)  <->  Hidden/Shader Graph/FallbackError (22)

Across 40 `weaponmodmaterials`: HDRP/Lit 23, MilkShaders/Lit-Template 9, MilkShaders/UERemap 5, Shader Graphs/RealisticScopeEffect 1, HDRP/Autodesk Interactive 1, Ultimate Scope Shaders/HolographicSight 1.

So the family split is real: character gear leans on the dev's own Shader Graph `MilkShaders/Lit-Template`, weapon parts lean on stock `HDRP/Lit`. Both expose the same HDRP Lit property block — PROVEN from a MilkShaders/Lit-Template material's saved properties: TexEnvs `_BaseColorMap`, `_MaskMap`, `_NormalMap`, `_DetailMap`, `_EmissiveColorMap` (+ `unity_Lightmaps`/`unity_LightmapsInd`/`unity_ShadowMasks`), Colors `_BaseColor`, `_EmissiveColor`, `_EmissiveColorLDR`, `_SpecularColor`, `_TransmittanceColor`, `_DiffusionProfileAsset`, Floats `_AORemapMin/_AORemapMax`, `_AlphaCutoff`, `_BumpScale`, `_CoatMask`, `_Anisotropy`, `_BASE_LAYER_TRIPLANAR`.

`_MainTex` shows up in 23/40 character and 24/40 weapon materials as a stale serialised slot, and `_AnisotropyMap` in ~20-23/40. Do not target `_MainTex` — the live slot is `_BaseColorMap`.

The FallbackError twin is exactly why `mat.shader = Shader.Find(mat.shader.name)` is required: the shader object is present but carries no compiled variants, so HDRP falls through to the error shader unless you rebind onto the player's compiled copy. Note the reference's warning applies here — MilkShaders/Lit-Template is a Shader Graph and Shader Graph shaders use their own property IDs, so never blind-swap an HDRP/Lit material onto it or vice versa.

findings.title: All textures stream to a .resS side-file — object-level byte patching writes nothing
findings.detail:
PROVEN: every Texture2D read from every sampled bundle has `image_data` of length 0 and `m_StreamData.path = archive:/CAB-<id>/CAB-<id>.resS`. Example from charactermodmaterials_assets_12x5aor2: `12x5 AOR2` 2048x2048 fmt 10, `Pouch_Ferro_GP_12x5_OCP_OpenGL_Normal` 1024x1024 fmt 12, `MaskMap` 512x512 fmt 12 — all three streamed to `archive:/CAB-ae9ca5272710d676757d0d706594cfd5/CAB-ae9ca5272710d676757d0d706594cfd5.resS`.

Format codes observed (Unity TextureFormat enum): 10 = DXT1/BC1 (base colour, no alpha), 12 = DXT5/BC3 (normals, most mask maps), 25 = BC7 (6 of 121 sampled character textures). Dimension histogram across 80 sampled material bundles: 2048x2048 x136, 1024x1024 x64, 512x512 x26, 2048x1024 x10, 256x256 x4. Mip chains are full (12/11/10 mips on the 2048/1024/512 trio).

The consequence for tooling: reading `Texture2D.image_data` gives you nothing, and writing to the Texture2D object alone changes nothing on screen. You must go through UnityPy's `set_image` / save path so it rewrites the .resS payload and the offset/size in m_StreamData.
findings.names: m_StreamData, archive:/CAB-<id>/CAB-<id>.resS, DXT1(10), DXT5(12), BC7(25)
findings.reskin: Author replacements at the shipped dimensions and formats (2048 BC1 base colour, 1024 BC3 normal, 512 BC3 mask) and let UnityPy regenerate mips. Changing dimensions is allowed but changing format from BC1 to BC3 doubles that texture's memory across every instance.

findings.title: LoadoutManager is an index registry with reference-counted, timer-deferred unloading
findings.detail:
PROVEN from the interop dump (D:\OperatorHSR\re\op\loadout_review_dump.txt lines 405-540). `Il2Cpp.LoadoutManager` is a `singleton`. The art registry is a set of INDEX-PARALLEL arrays:

  AllStrippedCharacterMods : Il2CppReferenceArray<AssetReferenceGameObject>
  CharacterModInfo         : Il2CppReferenceArray<CharacterModInfo>      (name/icon/slot, no bundle load)
  CharacterModCompatibilityCache : Il2CppStringArray
  AllStrippedWeaponMods    : Il2CppReferenceArray<AssetReferenceGameObject>
  WeaponModInfo            : Il2CppReferenceArray<WeaponModInfo>
  WeaponModCompatibilityCache : Il2CppStringArray

That parallelism is the useful part: `CharacterModInfo[i]` gives you ModName, DisplayName, UiIcon, ModSlot, CharacterSlot, isLocked/unlockKey/unlockReason WITHOUT triggering the addressable load. You can enumerate the entire catalogue of items cheaply and only load the ones you touch.

Refcount state:
  LoadedCharacterMods : Dictionary<int,int>   (index -> live instance count)
  LoadedWeaponMods    : Dictionary<int,int>
  CharacterModsToUnload : List<int>
  WeaponModsToUnload    : List<int>

Lifecycle methods: `RegisterCharacterModInstance(int)` / `CharacterModDestroyed(int)` and `RegisterWeaponModInstance(int)` / `WeaponModInstanceDestroyed(int)` move the counters; `CheckForUnUsedAddressable(AddressableObjectType type, int index) -> IEnumerator` is a COROUTINE, so the unload is deferred by a timer rather than immediate; `AddressablesUnloadTime : float` and `SetAddressableAssetUnloadTime(float)` set that grace period; `UnloadAddressable(AssetReferenceGameObject argo, AddressableObjectType type, int index)` does the release.

Lookup helpers: `find_characterMod(string) -> int`, `find_attachment(string) -> int`, `GetNumCharacterMods()`, `GetNumWeaponMods()`, `GetCharacterMod(int) -> CharacterMod`, `GetCharacterMod(string) -> CharacterMod`, `GetWeaponMod(int) -> GameObject`, `GetAttachment(string) -> GameObject`. Also `PlaceholderMaterial : Material`, `SingleStrippedWeaponModCreationID : int`, `SceneChanged()`, `OnLoad()`.

NEEDS-PROBE: `GetCharacterMod(int)` returns a `CharacterMod` synchronously, which for an addressable means either a blocking `WaitForCompletion` or reading `.Asset` off an already-completed handle. `WaitForCompletion` does appear in global-metadata (identifiers.txt line 107837, plus `<WaitForCompletion>d__15`, `InternalWaitForCompletion`, `InvokeWaitForCompletion`, `SetWaitForCompletionCallback`) but those are Unity's own Addressables members — this does not prove Assembly-CSharp calls it. Probe: hook `LoadoutManager.GetCharacterMod(int)` and log elapsed ms on a cold index; a multi-ms first call means a synchronous blocking load, sub-microsecond means preloaded handles.

NEEDS-PROBE: the `AddressableObjectType` enum members. It is not a top-level type in the Il2Cpp namespace (InteropInspector returned 0 matching types for both `^Il2Cpp\.AddressableObjectType$` and `^AddressableObjectType$`), so it is nested or otherwise namespaced. Settle with `Enum.GetNames` at runtime; usage implies exactly two values (character vs weapon).

+-- index i  (the one true id for a character item)
|     +-- AllStrippedCharacterMods[i] : AssetReferenceGameObject  -> GUID -> bundle
|     +-- CharacterModInfo[i]         : ModName/DisplayName/UiIcon/ModSlot   (FREE, no load)

(1) Raise `SetAddressableAssetUnloadTime(large)` while iterating so bundles stay resident and you can keep re-reading the loaded Material instead of racing the unload coroutine. (2) Walk `CharacterModInfo[]` to build a full name->index map with zero disk cost, then `find_characterMod(name)` to jump straight to the index whose bundle you want to edit.

findings.title: THE BIG ASYMMETRY: WeaponMod has the addressable lifecycle but NO material path at all — weapon colourways cannot be mutated at runtime
findings.detail:
PROVEN by dumping both types. `Il2Cpp.CharacterMod` and `Il2Cpp.WeaponMod` share an identical addressable lifecycle:
  SetAssetReferenceIndex(int), AssetReferenceIndex, TryInitAssetRef(), DestroyAssetRef(), _assetRefInit, _assetRefDestroy, LogAdDestroyWarning
(`Ad` = Addressable; the Log* flags are double-register/double-destroy diagnostics. CharacterMod also has `LogAdSpawnWarning`; WeaponMod has only the Destroy one.)

WeaponMod additionally carries `MyModIndex`, `AmmoReferenceIndex` and `_repackedMagInit` — a SECOND addressable reference on the same component for the loaded ammo/mag.

But `WeaponMod` has NO `material`, NO `materialIndex`, NO `materialBaseColourReference`, NO `modifyColour`, NO `textureModifer`, NO `baseColour`, NO `rendToModify`, NO `ActuallySetMaterial()`, NO `ApplyColorModifier()`. Its only non-addressable methods are `startInteraction(int)`, `ForceInteraction(int)`, `ZeroTransform(...)`, `OnDestroy()`.

This is the single most consequential fact in this area. The game's runtime recolour machinery exists ONLY on the character side. A weapon attachment's finish is decided entirely by which prefab (and therefore which material bundle) was loaded — there is no hook to intercept, no index to bump, no colour to set. Every FDE/BLK/black weapon-part variant is a separate authored prefab + material bundle pair (which is why weaponmodmaterials colourway tokens are so sparse: blk 14, fde 8, black 6, versus 40 coyote / 28 black / 28 mc on the character side).

Meaning: **weapon reskins are a bundle-editing job, full stop.** Character reskins have both options.

findings.title: The character material path: materialBaseColourReference is a shader property NAME, and rendToModify is a single Renderer
findings.detail:
PROVEN signatures on `Il2Cpp.CharacterMod`:
  modifyColour : bool          textureModifer : bool   (SHIPPED TYPO — 'Modifer', not 'Modifier')
  materialIndex : int          material : Material
  materialBaseColourReference : string
  baseColour : Texture2D       rendToModify : Renderer
  tattooMaterial : Material    isSkinned : bool / isSkinnedisPatch : bool
  skinnedMesh : SkinnedMeshRenderer / skinnedMeshes : SkinnedMeshRenderer[]
  ApplyColorModifier() -> void         ActuallySetMaterial() -> void

EVIDENCE that `materialBaseColourReference` holds a shader property name rather than an asset name: I searched Assembly-CSharp's string-literal table (D:\OperatorHSR\re\op\literals.txt) for `_BaseColorMap`, `_BaseColor`, `_MainTex`, `_MaskMap`, `_EmissiveColor` — the ONLY hits are `_Color` (line 18526) and the `_EmissiveColor`/`_EmissiveColorLDR`/`_EmissiveColorHDR`/`_EmissiveColorMap` cluster at line 26374, both of which read as HDRP/Unity-side literals, not game code. No HDRP texture-slot name is hard-coded in game code. So the property name has to arrive as serialised per-prefab data, and `materialBaseColourReference` is the only string field on CharacterMod shaped to carry it. Marked LIKELY, not proven — the settling probe is to enumerate every `CharacterMod` prefab in `AllStrippedCharacterMods` and log `materialBaseColourReference`; if the values read `_BaseColorMap`/`_BaseColor` the case is closed.

`rendToModify` is a SINGLE `Renderer`, not an array. Items whose visual spans several renderers will only have one recoloured by `ApplyColorModifier()`. That is a real authored limitation you will hit.

`CharacterModParent.IsColorModSlot : bool` marks which sockets are colour-modifier slots — the UI-side gate on whether the colour path is offered at all.

The colour data is actually in use: sampling `_BaseColor` across 40 charactermodmaterials found (1,1,1,1) x30 but also (0.91,0.91,0.91,1) x10, (0.12,0.12,0.12,1) and (0.31,0.31,0.25,1); across 40 weaponmodmaterials (1,1,1,1) x21, (0.91,0.91,0.91,1) x14, plus 0.71 / 0.47 / 0.45 / 0.03 greys. findings.title: Shared-material hazard: CharacterMod.material is a bundle asset, so mutating it is process-wide and outlives the character
findings.detail:
The materials in question are single Material objects inside addressable bundles (PROVEN: 39/40 and 40/40 sampled material bundles contain exactly one Material). `CharacterMod` is a component on an addressable PREFAB (`AllStrippedCharacterMods` is an array of `AssetReferenceGameObject`). So `CharacterMod.material` points at the bundle's shared Material asset, not a per-instance copy.

What that means concretely:
- `charMod.material.SetTexture("_BaseColorMap", myTex)` mutates the loaded asset. Every character in the session wearing that item changes, including remote players' rendered copies, including the loadout preview mannequin.
- The mutation persists as long as the bundle stays loaded, i.e. until the refcount hits zero AND the `AddressablesUnloadTime` coroutine fires. It survives the death of the CharacterMod that you mutated through.
- It also survives across scenes if anything keeps the refcount above zero.
- When the bundle IS finally unloaded and reloaded, your mutation is gone. So a runtime reskin needs re-application, not one-shot application.

PROVEN about the API surface: `CharacterMod` exposes only whole-Material handles — `material`, `tattooMaterial`, `rendToModify` (a Renderer) — and no MaterialPropertyBlock member of any kind. The game never uses per-renderer property blocks on this path; it assigns Materials wholesale. So there is no built-in per-instance escape hatch.

The safe pattern for a runtime mod is therefore YOUR OWN code, not the game's: touch `Renderer.material` (Unity instantiates a private copy on first access, scoped to that renderer) or set a `MaterialPropertyBlock` via `Renderer.SetPropertyBlock`. Never `Renderer.sharedMaterial`, and never the `CharacterMod.material` handle, if you want the change scoped to one character. Caveat on MaterialPropertyBlock under HDRP: it breaks SRP batching for that renderer, and against `MilkShaders/Lit-Template` you are addressing Shader Graph property IDs, which the reference explicitly warns do not match HDRP/Lit's.

Also relevant: `LoadoutManager.PlaceholderMaterial : Material` is what stands in while a stripped prefab's material bundle is still resolving or fails — if a swapped bundle shows up as a flat untextured surface rather than magenta, you are looking at PlaceholderMaterial, which means the load failed rather than the shader failed.

And `LoadoutManager.CurrentTextureQuality : int`, `TextureQualityChanged()`, `OnTextureQualityIncreased : Action` — the game reloads texture detail on a quality change. A runtime texture swap must re-apply on `OnTextureQualityIncreased` or it will be reverted when the player raises texture quality.

findings.reskin: If you mutate at runtime, subscribe to `OnTextureQualityIncreased` and re-apply, and copy to `Renderer.material` per instance unless you actually want every character changed at once. A flat grey item after a swap means PlaceholderMaterial and a failed load; magenta means a live shader that failed to rebind. Two different bugs, two different fixes.

PROVEN by set-intersecting the slug namespaces from live filenames. Of 1,025 `charactermodmaterials` slugs and 1,203 `weaponmodmaterials` slugs, exactly TWO appear in both: `blk` and `body`. Of 1,165 `charactermods_stripped` and 1,581 `weaponmods_stripped` slugs, ZERO overlap.

  loaded in the gun (weaponmodmaterials): `magazine_pmag30_genm3`
No shared substring you could grep for reliably. The character side favours `MI_`-prefixed, product-named CGTrader material-instance names (598 of 1,025 are `MI_`); the weapon side overwhelmingly uses the raw source-mesh material name (1,117 of 1,203 unprefixed) — hence `magazine`, `magazine1`, `magazine2`, `magazine3`, `magazine_mat`, `magazine_20r`, `magazine_20rtransluent` (shipped typo, one 's'), `magazine_ext`, `magazine_50`, `magazine_75rnd`, `magazine_hk_gen2_30`, `magazine_hk_standart_30` (shipped typo, 'standart').

findings.title: When to edit a bundle versus mutate at runtime
findings.detail:
EDIT THE BUNDLE when: (a) the target is a weapon attachment — there is no runtime material API on WeaponMod at all, so this is the only option; (b) you want the change to be permanent, correct in the loadout preview, correct on remote players' rendered copies, and free of per-frame cost; (c) you are changing texture CONTENT (camo pattern, mask map, normal) rather than a tint; (d) you want it to survive a texture-quality change and a bundle unload/reload cycle. Cost: you must repack the shipped bundle (preserve the internal GUID name), write through UnityPy so the .resS stream is rewritten, and re-scan + rename to the current 32-hex hash after every game patch. The GIGN precedent (10 charactermodmaterials bundles) proves this route ships and works.

MUTATE AT RUNTIME when: (a) the target is character gear AND you want it conditional — per-character, per-team, per-mission, toggleable; (b) you want to iterate without a game restart; (c) you are only changing a tint or swapping between materials that already exist. Cost: it is a shared-material world, so scope your writes to `Renderer.material` or a `MaterialPropertyBlock` on your own component, never through `CharacterMod.material`; re-apply on `LoadoutManager.OnTextureQualityIncreased`; and hold the bundle resident with `SetAddressableAssetUnloadTime` while you work or the unload coroutine pulls the asset out from under you.

HYBRID, and the best of the three for a camo project: edit bundles for the art, and use the runtime `materialIndex` path only to make new colourways SELECTABLE. Variants of one item already share a ModName and differ only by `materialIndex`, so an added colourway needs a new material bundle plus an index the UI can reach — not new code on the render path.

Do NOT try to load a brand-new bundle at runtime as the primary route. The reference is explicit that AssetBundles only load here through a raw `il2cpp_runtime_invoke` on `LoadFromFileAsync_Internal` (managed entry points fail on span marshalling), and materials come back needing `mat.shader = Shader.Find(mat.shader.name)` — the FallbackError twin finding above shows exactly why. Replacing a shipped bundle in place sidesteps every bit of that, because the game's own loader does the work.
