findings.title: Magenta-under-HDRP traps, corrected: Mobile/Particles/* is not in the build at all, and the three FallbackError shaders are shipped inside every art bundle
findings.detail:
Registry check across all 351 names:
  Mobile/*  -> ZERO matches. Shader.Find("Mobile/Particles/Additive") returns NULL, so material.shader = null
               and Unity substitutes its internal error shader. This is a harder failure than the brief
               assumed (it said they resolve then render magenta) — you get null, not a bound shader.
  Legacy Shaders/Particles/Additive              props: _TintColor, _MainTex, _InvFade
  Legacy Shaders/Particles/Alpha Blended         props: _TintColor, _MainTex, _InvFade
  Legacy Shaders/Particles/Alpha Blended Premultiply  props: _MainTex, _InvFade
  Legacy Shaders/VertexLit                       props: _Color, _SpecColor, _Emission, _Shininess, _MainTex
  Particles/Standard Unlit (30 props, m_FallbackName = "VertexLit")
  -> these four DO resolve via Shader.Find but are built-in-render-pipeline shaders. Under HDRP they draw
     magenta. Note Particles/Standard Unlit falls back to VertexLit, which is also built-in — the fallback
     chain never reaches anything HDRP can draw.

The magenta shaders themselves, all shipped and all present inside art bundles:
  Hidden/Shader Graph/FallbackError   pathID 3819691914921817934, blob 525 B  (Shader Graph materials)
  Hidden/Core/FallbackError           pathID -8015457887526078469, blob 525 B
  Hidden/HDRP/FallbackError           pathID 1354542265007958578, blob 1496 B
  Hidden/InternalErrorShader          named as m_FallbackName by the three Vefects URP-authored shaders
                                      (SH_Vefects_URP_Candle_Flame_01, _Candle_Smoke_01,
                                       SH_Vefects_HDRP_VFX_Muzzle_Flash)
Which fallback a broken material lands on tells you the family it came from: Shader Graph -> Hidden/Shader
Graph/FallbackError, hand-written HDRP -> Hidden/HDRP/FallbackError, SRP core -> Hidden/Core/FallbackError.
findings.names: Legacy Shaders/Particles/Additive, Particles/Standard Unlit, Hidden/Shader Graph/FallbackError, Hidden/Core/FallbackError, Hidden/HDRP/FallbackError, Hidden/InternalErrorShader
findings.reskin: For a custom particle effect use Vefects/SH_Vefects_HDRP_VFX_Opaque_Particle_01, Knife/HDRP Particle, Knife/HDRP Particle Lit Setup, or Shader Graphs/ParticleLit (60 props) — never Legacy Shaders/Particles/*. If your imported VFX is magenta, that is why.

findings.title: Texture payload reality: BaseColor is DXT1 (no alpha), Normal and MaskMap are DXT5, pixels live in a separate resS stream
findings.detail:
PROVEN by reading every Texture2D in the 34 sampled bundles.
Formats (Unity TextureFormat enum): 12 = DXT5/BC3 x57, 10 = DXT1/BC1 x40, 25 = BC7 x2.
Dimensions: 2048x2048 x59, 1024x1024 x30, 512x512 x8, 4096x4096 x1, 1000x1000 x1.
Example sizes confirm the format read: watch_low_body_BaseMap 2048x2048 fmt=10 mips=12 colorSpace=1 (sRGB)
size=2796216 B; watch_low_body_Normal 2048x2048 fmt=12 mips=12 colorSpace=0 (linear) size=5592432 B.
Biggest observed: cryeg2g3_MI_CRYE_LS_Normal 4096x4096 DXT5 mips=13 = 22369648 B.

Every texture has m_StreamData.path = 'archive:/CAB-<hash>/CAB-<hash>.resS' — the pixel bytes are NOT in the
asset record, they are in a sibling .resS stream inside the bundle. A hex-edit of the asset file will not
replace an image; you must rewrite the resS (UnityPy's set_image does this).

Naming grammar recovered from the texture names, and it is consistent enough to script against:
  <asset>_<MaterialName>_BaseMap | _Normal | _NormalOpenGL | _MaskMap
  older/Unreal-sourced sets instead use _BaseColor, _Roughness, _Metalness, _Normal (feeds MilkShaders/UERemap)
Observed: watch_low_body_{BaseMap,Normal,MaskMap}; cryeg2g3_MI_CRYE_LS_{BaseMap,Normal};
backpacks_MI_AVS_Zipon_bag_BaseMap; batterypacks_MI_SuperHighCut_Ac_BaseMap; AVS_bag_{Roughness,Normal,Metalness};
JPC_MC_{BaseColor,Normal}; Pouch_Ferro_GP_12x5_OCP_OpenGL_Normal; GatorZ_Magnum_Normal; Reticle01;
and bare colourway names for the Milk pouches: '12x5 AOR2', '12x5 BLK', '12x5 MCB'.
findings.names: _BaseColorMap, _MaskMap, _NormalMap, _MainTex, DXT1, DXT5, BC7, m_StreamData, .resS
findings.tree:
a gear material's texture slots (30 of 34 sampled materials carry exactly these three)
├─ _BaseColorMap   DXT1, sRGB, 2048² typical      <- albedo. NO ALPHA CHANNEL (DXT1)
│                  also aliased to _MainTex on HDRP/Lit materials (same PPtr, proven on 'body')
├─ _MaskMap        DXT5, linear, 512²-2048²       <- HDRP packed: R=Metallic G=AO B=DetailMask A=Smoothness
└─ _NormalMap      DXT5, linear, 1024²-4096²      <- note the '_OpenGL' suffix on some source names:
                                                     those are +Y green, the rest are DirectX -Y
optional, seen on 27/34: _DetailMap, _EmissiveColorMap
reticles only: _Reticle (Reticle01, 1024² DXT5, sRGB)
findings.reskin: Camo work is: replace _BaseColorMap, optionally repaint _MaskMap's A (smoothness) so wet/dry reads right, leave _NormalMap alone. Because _BaseColorMap is DXT1 you cannot add cutout alpha by editing the texture alone — you would have to re-import as DXT5/BC7 and enable _AlphaCutoffEnable.

findings.title: The keyword trap: adding a texture to an HDRP/Lit material does nothing unless the matching keyword is in m_ValidKeywords
findings.detail:
PROVEN from the material typetrees. m_ValidKeywords is serialized per material:
  'body' (HDRP/Lit)              -> ['_DISABLE_SSR_TRANSPARENT','_MASKMAP','_NORMALMAP','_NORMALMAP_TANGENT_SPACE'], m_CustomRenderQueue 2225
  '12x5 AOR2' (Lit-Template)     -> ['_DISABLE_SSR_TRANSPARENT'] only, m_CustomRenderQueue 2225
  'MI_CRYE_LS_MCWORN' (ClothWind)-> ['_DISABLE_SSR_TRANSPARENT'] only
  'mrs_reticle' (HolographicSight)-> ['_BLURRETICLE','_DISABLE_SSR_TRANSPARENT','_ENABLE_FOG_ON_TRANSPARENT','_SURFACE_TYPE_TRANSPARENT','_USERADIALNOISE'], m_CustomRenderQueue 3000
HDRP/Lit branches on _MASKMAP / _NORMALMAP / _NORMALMAP_TANGENT_SPACE / _DETAIL_MAP / _EMISSIVE_COLOR_MAP at
compile time. Setting mat.SetTexture("_MaskMap", t) on a material whose m_ValidKeywords lacks '_MASKMAP'
binds the texture and changes nothing on screen. The Shader Graph shaders (MilkShaders/*, ClothWind) do not
gate on those keywords — they read the sampler unconditionally — which is why the Milk materials carry only
_DISABLE_SSR_TRANSPARENT. On HolographicSight the feature toggles are BOTH a float property
(_BLURRETICLE, _USERADIALNOISE, _USE_OFFSET_NOISE, _USE_QUAD_CLIP, _USE_TEXTURE_COLOR) and a keyword; you
must set both or the branch stays compiled out.
findings.names: m_ValidKeywords, _MASKMAP, _NORMALMAP, _NORMALMAP_TANGENT_SPACE, _DISABLE_SSR_TRANSPARENT, _SURFACE_TYPE_TRANSPARENT, _BLURRETICLE, _USERADIALNOISE
findings.reskin: When authoring a bundle by hand, edit m_ValidKeywords alongside m_SavedProperties, and prefer EnableKeyword()+SetFloat() together at runtime. A MilkShaders/* target avoids the whole class of problem — that is a real reason to retarget a reskin onto Lit-Template rather than HDRP/Lit.

findings.detail:
PROVEN by scanning all 1,165 `charactermods_stripped` prefab bundles (16 s) for GameObjects whose name contains "patch", then reading the raw MonoBehaviour bytes on the hits. 488 of 1,165 garment prefabs carry patch geometry or a patch socket. The socket is a `CharacterModParent` MonoBehaviour (208-212 bytes, script-hash prefix `VEMk`) whose two serialized strings are `ModParentName` (the UI label) and `Mod_Compatibility`. Every patch socket in the game reads `Mod_Compatibility = "Patch"`. The item side is a `CharacterMod` MonoBehaviour (264 bytes) whose only string is `Compatibility = "Patch"`. That single token is the entire acceptance test — it is why any patch fits any patch socket, and it is why a custom patch needs nothing but that string to be socketable. For contrast, the adjacent socket on the same AVS vest reads `ModParentName="Armor Plates" / Mod_Compatibility="ArmourPlate"`.

The raw GameObject names are polluted by Unity's FBX-merge concatenation (e.g. `PCU Jacket Grey_PCU Jacket Grey_Rubgy Long Tucked FDE_..._MOD_LeftArmPatch (1)`). Ignore them. `ModParentName` inside the MonoBehaviour is the clean label the UI shows.

findings.title: The prefab does NOT hold the patch material — an AssetReference GUID does, and that is the whole reskin seam
findings.detail:
PROVEN. Every patch prefab I opened — all 12 Patreon patches, all 4 country/JTAC patches, all 4 DEVGRU patches — has its MeshRenderer's single material slot pointing at the IDENTICAL external PPtr `(m_FileID=2, m_PathID=-5343436609273763532)`, which resolves into the shared CAB `CAB-5b00af9b95ebb9aec2086aa927439000` / `CAB-62081254e5f53c3d16f8fcf3c684729f` that every character prefab depends on. It is a placeholder. The real material is carried as a 96-byte MonoBehaviour holding one 32-hex Addressables GUID, unique per patch: `'USA IR` -> 3d096450453969243b1e553816a62196; Patreon `Syko` -> f410575cb61a5b948bfe96a3803aaa4d; Patreon `AP_Amazing` -> dcb6795e1f234684c85d85d5a18901a0; Patreon `big_mamas_house` -> de8118d39bd12984588922ab8403bd42; CRYE G2 Shirt AOR1 -> 0ec6999e86065ca4d89d11e24d8a41cb. That is `CharacterMod.AssetReferenceIndex` + an AssetReference, loaded by Addressables and assigned by `CharacterMod.ActuallySetMaterial()` at runtime.

Consequence: editing a patch prefab bundle is pointless and editing the shared CAB would hit every garment in the game. The ONLY correct edit target is the `charactermodmaterials_assets_mi_patch_*` bundle. A vest by comparison carries an 860-byte MonoBehaviour with a list of 16 material GUIDs — that is what `materialIndex` indexes into; patches have exactly one, so patches have no colourway variants at runtime.

findings.title: Every patch texture, resolution and format — and the mipmap bug shipped on five of them
findings.detail:
PROVEN by UnityPy (config.FALLBACK_UNITY_VERSION="6000.3.8f1"; UnityPy 1.25.2, which I had to `pip install` — it was not present). All textures are BC-compressed; base colours are BC1 (DXT1, no alpha), normals and masks are BC3 (DXT5) except two BC1 normals. Five base colours ship with `m_MipCount = 1` — no mip chain at all. At any distance those patches will alias and shimmer. Four of the nine materials also carry no `_MaskMap` at all, so they get flat default AO/metal/smoothness.

The US-flag mask texture exists three times, under three different names, at three different resolutions, in three different bundles: `MaskMap` 2048 BC3, `patchusmask` 1024 BC3, `patch_us_mask` 512 BC3. And `Patch_US_IR_Normal` exists three times as three different assets — 2048 BC3 mips=12 (in mi_patch_us_bw1), 1024 BC3 mips=11 (in mi_patch_us_ir), 1024 BC1 mips=11 (in mi_patch_3dma_us_ir). Name-based batch replacement across bundles will without warning write the wrong resolution.

findings.title: There is a live IR-glow system: an IRPatch MonoBehaviour and an emissive material shipped with intensity zeroed
findings.detail:
PROVEN in two independent places. (1) `MI_Patch_US_BW 1` is the only patch material in the game with `_EmissiveColorMap` bound (to the 1024 BC1 texture `Patch_US_IR`) and the only one with `_UseEmissiveIntensity = 1.0`. But its `_EmissiveIntensity = 0.0`, `_EmissiveExposureWeight = 0.0` and `_EmissiveColor = (0,0,0,0)`. The glow is fully authored and switched off at rest. findings.title: The exact modder recipe, three routes, with the two traps that kill each
findings.detail:
Route A — texture swap, no code, precedent already shipped (the French GIGN pack did exactly this on 10 charactermodmaterials bundles).
  1. Re-scan the LIVE folder for the current filename. The 32-hex suffix is a content hash that changes every game patch; a bundle sitting under an old hash is simply never loaded and your mod without warning does nothing. This is the single most common failure.
  2. `pip install UnityPy` (it is NOT installed on this machine by default — I installed 1.25.2). Set `UnityPy.config.FALLBACK_UNITY_VERSION = "6000.3.8f1"`; the bundles are version-stripped and UnityPy will warn and fall back.
  3. Open the bundle, find the Texture2D by name, `img.image = new_pil_image; img.save()`, then write `env.file.save()` back over the same filename.
  4. Match dimensions and format exactly (see the texture tree). The game does not verify bundle content hashes, so a renamed/edited bundle loads fine.

Route B — new patch item. You cannot add an Addressables catalog entry without rewriting catalog.bin. Instead hijack an existing Patreon patch: its prefab already has the CustomPatch mesh, `Compatibility="Patch"`, and a unique material GUID. Repaint that material's textures and the item becomes yours, keeping its name in the UI unless you also edit the prefab's DisplayNameOverride.

Route C — MelonLoader, runtime. Postfix `CharacterMod.ActuallySetMaterial()`, branch on `Compatibility == "Patch"` or on `modSlot`, and assign a Material you built yourself. Trap: the material that comes out of a bundle has a broken shader reference and must be repaired with `mat.shader = Shader.Find(name)` — but the shader name is EMPTY in the shipped bundle (I read `m_Shader` on all 9 patch materials and every one resolved to an empty-name Shader object), so you cannot recover the original name from the file. You must supply it.
findings.names: UnityPy 1.25.2, FALLBACK_UNITY_VERSION 6000.3.8f1, CharacterMod.ActuallySetMaterial, CharacterMod.Compatibility, Shader.Find
findings.reskin: This is the actionable core. Route A on mi_patch_us_ir + mi_patch_us_bw + mi_patch_3dma_us_co covers every US flag patch a player can equip, for about an hour of work.

findings.title: The patch family uses at least TWO different shaders, and neither name survives in the bundle
findings.detail:
PROVEN by property-set comparison. Eight of the nine patch materials carry the full HDRP/Lit property set — `_SubsurfaceMaskMap`, `_TransmissionMaskMap`, `_TransmittanceColorMap`, `_IridescenceThicknessMap`, `_IridescenceMaskMap`, `_CoatMaskMap`, `_TangentMapOS`, `_NormalMapOS`, `_ThicknessMap`, `_DiffusionProfileHash`, `_MaterialID`, `_ZTestGBuffer`, `_StencilRef`. `MI_Patch_3DMA_US_CO` does NOT: it is missing all of those and instead carries `_BASE_LAYER_TRIPLANAR`, `_DETAIL_TRIPLANAR_UV`, `_HeightMapParametrization`, `_HeightPoMAmplitude`, `_DisplacementLockObjectScale`, `_DisplacementLockTilingScale`. That is a layered/triplanar shader, not stock HDRP/Lit — the candidates are HDRP/LayeredLit or the dev's own `MilkShaders/*` family.

All nine materials also bind both `_BaseColorMap` and `_MainTex` to the SAME texture (except MI_Patch_3DMA_US_CO which binds only `_BaseColorMap`). That is the HDRP/Lit legacy alias being written by the importer, not two separate slots.

findings.title: Addressables performs NO integrity check on these bundles - the per-bundle CRC field is zero
findings.detail:
This was the decisive open question. Answer: an edited bundle is accepted.

Evidence chain, all read from files:

1. D:\OperatorHSR\re\op\aa_settings.json: Addressables 2.8.1, m_CatalogLocations points at a single LOCAL catalog.bin via ContentCatalogProvider, m_IsLocalCatalogInBundle=false, m_CertificateHandlerType is EMPTY (no assembly, no class), m_ExtraInitializationData empty, no remote catalog entry at all. There is no signing handler and nothing to sign against.

2. literals.txt confirms the binary-catalog reader is present:
   UnityEngine.AddressableAssets.ResourceLocators.ContentCatalogData|AssetBundleRequestOptionsSerializationAdapter
   ...ContentCatalogData+AssetBundleRequestOptionsSerializationAdapter+|Common
   ...ContentCatalogData+AssetBundleRequestOptionsSerializationAdapter|SerializedData
   That adapter is the struct that would carry Crc.

3. I located the per-bundle record inside catalog.bin by anchoring on each bundle's real on-disk file size as a little-endian uint32, then read the uint32 immediately preceding it. Across all 4,989 bundles:
     size-as-u32 located for 4979, not located for 10, ambiguous (>1 hit) for 241
     field immediately BEFORE size == 0 for 4903
     nonzero for 76, and every nonzero value is a near-unique singleton (top counts 3,2,2,2,2) which is the signature of a coincidental match inside the 241 ambiguous set, not a real CRC column.
   So the Crc column is 0. 'Use Asset Bundle CRC' was off at build time.

4. Cross-checked the record layout on two bundles. For 12x5aor2 (size 3788514) and 12x5blk (size 3594078) the u32 windows are structurally identical:
     [..., <localoff>, <localoff>, 0, SIZE, 82846, 82911, <off>, NAMEOFF, <off>, 0x40004181, 0xFFFFFFFF]
   NAMEOFF is the exact byte offset where the full bundle FILENAME string lives (83368 for aor2, 83715 for blk - verified by independent string search). 82846/82911 are shared by both records = the pooled Common struct. The 0 sits in the Crc slot in both.

5. All 4,989 bundle filenames are present verbatim as strings in catalog.bin (missing for 0). The raw 16-byte content hash is also present for 4,967 of them - that is the AssetBundleRequestOptions.Hash used for remote-bundle CACHING only; it is not verified for a local LoadFromFileAsync.

6. catalog.hash exists (e2b0cde1008ba450acc9abaf9cb80d53) but with no remote catalog configured it is only compared against a remote catalog that does not exist. Editing a bundle does not change catalog.hash anyway.

7. Empirical corroboration already in hand: the shipped French GIGN retexture pack of 10 charactermodmaterials bundles works.

RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY: my field identification is offset-inference, not a full binary-catalog parse. If you want it airtight the runtime probe is a MelonLoader Harmony postfix on UnityEngine.ResourceManagement.ResourceProviders.AssetBundleRequestOptions get_Crc (or just log options.Crc in AssetBundleResource.BeginOperation) and print BundleName+Crc for the first 20 loads. That is a 15-line mod.

You do NOT need to touch catalog.bin, you do NOT need to recompute anything, and you do NOT need to keep the file size the same (my repack grew the file 57% and the catalog's stale BundleSize is not enforced for local loads). The only identity that must match is the FILENAME.

findings.title: Complete safe edit path, with the real commands, proven end to end on 12x5 BLK
findings.detail:
Every step below was executed except the final in-game launch.

STEP 0 - environment. UnityPy was NOT installed; I installed it. Confirmed working: UnityPy 1.25.2 with Pillow present, under (local path)  python -m pip install UnityPy
  # in every script: UnityPy.config.FALLBACK_UNITY_VERSION="6000.3.8f1"
  # bundles are version-stripped: BundleFile reports signature=UnityFS, version=8,
  # version_engine='0.0.0', version_player='5.x.x'. Without the fallback UnityPy warns
  # (UnityVersionFallbackWarning) and can misparse.

STEP 1 - locate the bundle for a visible item. The slug is DERIVABLE from the material name, no guessing:
    slug = material asset name, lowercased, spaces deleted, underscores kept, '.mat' dropped
  Verified against four independent cases:
    '12x5 BLK.mat'            -> charactermodmaterials_assets_12x5blk_...
    'MI_Patch_JTAC.mat'       -> charactermodmaterials_assets_mi_patch_jtac_...
    'MI_Patch_US_BW 1.mat'    -> charactermodmaterials_assets_mi_patch_us_bw1_...
    'acog_reticle.mat'        -> weaponmodmaterials_assets_acog_reticle_...
  Material names come from D:\OperatorHSR\re\op\catalog_strings.txt (grep it).
  Then resolve the live hash:
    Get-ChildItem 'D:\Games\OPERATOR\OPERATOR_Data\StreamingAssets\aa\StandaloneWindows64' -Filter 'charactermodmaterials_assets_12x5blk_*.bundle'

STEP 2 - back up. Copy the original out of the game folder BEFORE editing. Steam 'Verify integrity of game files' restores originals, which is your undo, but a Steam depot update will also without warning revert your mod with no warning.

STEP 3 - unpack / edit / repack, all in one UnityPy pass (do not extract to disk and rebuild):
  import UnityPy, os, shutil
  UnityPy.config.FALLBACK_UNITY_VERSION="6000.3.8f1"
  shutil.copy(SRC, "work.bundle")
  env = UnityPy.load("work.bundle")
  for o in env.objects:
      if o.type.name == "Texture2D":
          d = o.read()
          if d.m_Name == "12x5 BLK":
              d.image.save("export.png")          # 2048x2048 RGBA, decoded from DXT1
              # ...paint export.png in your editor...
              img = Image.open("new.png").convert("RGBA")
              d.set_image(img, target_format=d.m_TextureFormat, mipmap_count=12)
              d.save()
  open("out.bundle","wb").write(env.file.save(packer="lz4"))

STEP 4 - install. Rename out.bundle to the CURRENT live filename (slug + current 32-hex hash) and drop it over the original. Do not rename the slug, do not invent a hash.

STEP 5 - verify. Reload with UnityPy first (cheap, catches a corrupt write), then in game. Reload proof from my run - all seven objects survived with correct names and the AssetBundle object kept its internal identity:
  [('Texture2D','12x5 BLK'), ('Shader',''), ('Texture2D','Pouch_Ferro_GP_12x5_OCP_OpenGL_Normal'),
   ('Texture2D','MaskMap'), ('AssetBundle','278610ccc33753685c688335d2868068.bundle'),
   ('Material','12x5 BLK'), ('Shader','')]
  CAB entries preserved exactly: CAB-891e8972622288d41e6ace56d8711a56 and its .resS.
  AssetBundle m_Container preserved, 1 entry:
   'Assets/1Assets/1CGTrader/3DMA/Ferro FCPC/PBR_Pouch_Ferro_GP_12x5_tx/Retextures/12x5 BLK.mat'

In game: the 12x5 pouch is a chest-rig CharacterMod, so verify in the loadout cabinet, not in a mission - faster iteration.

findings.title: UnityPy repack without warning DESTROYS THE MIP CHAIN unless you pass mipmap_count
findings.detail:
This is the highest-value trap in the workflow and it produces no error.

Proven by measurement. Original 12x5 BLK: m_MipCount=12, streamed 2,796,216 bytes in the .resS.

  Using the obvious API, d.image = new_img; d.save():
     reloaded -> m_MipCount = 1, image_data = 2,097,152 bytes
     2048*2048/2 = 2,097,152 exactly = ONE DXT1 level, no chain.

  Using d.set_image(img, target_format=d.m_TextureFormat, mipmap_count=12):
     reloaded -> m_MipCount = 10, image_data = 2,796,200 bytes
     Verified self-consistent: 2048..4 px DXT1 chain sums to exactly 2,796,200.
     16 bytes short of the original 2,796,216 because UnityPy stops at the 4x4 DXT block
     and omits the padded 2x2 and 1x1 levels (8 bytes each). Harmless.

So: the image setter gives you mips 1; set_image with mipmap_count gives you a correct 10-level chain. In game the mips-1 version shimmers badly at distance, costs 2 MB resident, and looks like 'my camo is noisy' rather than 'my tool broke'.

FORMAT IS PRESERVED. target_format=d.m_TextureFormat round-tripped fmt 10 (DXT1/BC1) correctly. Do not let UnityPy pick - always pass the original format back.

NOT EVERY TEXTURE NEEDS THIS. Several shipped textures already have mips 1, so for those the naive setter is fine:
  Patch_JTAC_BaseColor 1024x1024 DXT1 mips 1
  chevon@4x (ACOG reticle) 2048x2048 DXT5 mips 1
Mip-chained ones seen: 12x5 BLK DXT1 mips 12, Pouch_..._Normal DXT5 mips 11, MaskMap DXT5 mips 10, jtac_mask DXT5 mips 10, Patch_JTAC_Normal DXT5 mips 10.

SIZE COST. Repacking inflates the bundle because UnityPy's lz4 is weaker than the shipped packing and the edited texture migrates out of the .resS into the serialized file (its m_StreamData.path becomes empty while untouched textures keep 'archive:/CAB-.../CAB-....resS'). Measured: 3,594,078 -> 5,090,416 (mips 1) and -> 5,633,468 (mips 10), about +42% to +57%. Both load fine. Budget ~1.5x disk per edited bundle.
findings.names: Texture2D.set_image, m_MipCount, m_StreamData, TextureFormat 10 (DXT1), TextureFormat 12 (DXT5)
findings.reskin: Always: d.set_image(img, target_format=d.m_TextureFormat, mipmap_count=<original m_MipCount>). Read and print the original m_MipCount first so you know whether the source even had a chain.

findings.title: The addressable is the MATERIAL, never the texture - and the shaders in every bundle have EMPTY names
findings.detail:
Two structural facts that decide what you are allowed to edit.

1. THE ADDRESSABLE KEY IS THE .mat. Every material bundle I opened has exactly ONE m_Container entry and it is a material path:
     12x5 BLK    -> 'Assets/1Assets/1CGTrader/3DMA/Ferro FCPC/PBR_Pouch_Ferro_GP_12x5_tx/Retextures/12x5 BLK.mat'
     MI_Patch_JTAC -> 'Assets/1Assets/1CGTrader/3DMA/WSF Operator V2/Textures/PATCHES/PBR_Patch_US_JTAC_tx/MI_Patch_JTAC.mat'
     acog_reticle  -> 'Assets/1Assets/1CGTrader/_FirearmRelated/Trijicon/TA31/acog_reticle.mat'
   The textures are unnamed dependencies riding inside the same bundle. Consequence: you never have to register anything, and the game's lookup key is untouched by a texture swap. It also means one bundle = one selectable item; you cannot add a second material to a bundle and have it appear.

2. SHADERS IN BUNDLES HAVE m_Name == ''. Every material bundle carries two Shader objects and both read back with an EMPTY name. In 12x5 BLK, 12x5 AOR2, 12x5 M81 - all identical: ('Shader',''), ('Shader',''). These are the stripped stubs left by the player build; the real shader comes from the built player at load. This sharpens the known rule: the documented fix mat.shader = Shader.Find(mat.shader.name) CANNOT work on these bundles, because Shader.Find("") returns null. That fix applies to bundles YOU build in an editor with named shaders, not to shipped ones.
   Practical rule: in a shipped bundle, edit Texture2D image data ONLY. Do not touch the Material, do not touch the Shader objects, do not change m_SavedProperties. Leave the binding alone and it keeps working, which is exactly why the GIGN precedent works.

3. THE ART IS BOUGHT ASSET-STORE/CGTRADER CONTENT. Paths reveal the source packs: '1Assets/1CGTrader/3DMA/Ferro FCPC' (the Ferro Concealable Plate Carrier), '1CGTrader/3DMA/WSF Operator V2' (patches), '1CGTrader/_FirearmRelated/Trijicon/TA31'. If you own the same packs you have the original PSD/substance sources and can author at full quality instead of repainting a DXT-decoded PNG.

4. SHIPPED TYPO in an asset name: the ACOG reticle texture is 'chevon@4x', not 'chevron'. Match it exactly.

Opened three siblings of the same physical pouch and compared contents:

    Texture2D '12x5 AOR2'                              2048x2048 DXT1 mips 12

  charactermodmaterials_assets_12x5m81_aabffcb9...  (3,710,473 B)
    Texture2D '12x5 M81' + the SAME two named support maps

The full live family is six bundles: 12x5aor2, 12x5blk, 12x5gray, 12x5m81, 12x5mcb, 12x5od.

Two things follow.

FIRST, the normal map is named 'Pouch_Ferro_GP_12x5_OCP_OpenGL_Normal' - it carries the OCP colourway in its name yet ships identically in the AOR2, BLK and M81 bundles. The name is a leftover from whichever variant was authored first. Do not read colourway meaning into support-map names; only the base colour texture, which is always named EXACTLY like its material, is per-variant.

SECOND, this is the cheapest possible camo project. You only ever repaint one 2048x2048 texture per variant, and the base colour name tells you which one without opening anything. Six edits gives you a complete replacement camo family that appears as six separate selectable options in the cabinet, using the game's own UI, with no code.

Also note 'OpenGL_Normal' in the name: this normal map is OpenGL convention (+Y up). If you ever author a replacement normal, use OpenGL, not DirectX, or the lighting inverts.

findings.title: What file replacement CANNOT do: it cannot add a new option, only repaint an existing one
findings.detail:
This is the hard boundary of the whole workflow and it is worth stating before anyone plans a project.

The catalog is fixed and binary. Each material bundle exposes exactly one addressable key (proven above, m_Container has 1 entry in every bundle I opened). Adding a seventh 12x5 colourway would require a new bundle AND a new catalog entry AND the character-customisation option list to reference it. catalog.bin is Addressables 2.8.1 binary format with absolute file offsets into a shared string region - I verified offsets are absolute (the NAMEOFF field 83368 pointed exactly at the filename string at byte 83368). Inserting a record shifts every downstream offset. Editing it by hand is not a beginner project and I would not recommend it at all.

So file replacement gives you N-for-N substitution: every camo you add costs you one you delete. A pack that replaces all six 12x5 colourways with six of your own is fine; a pack that ADDS a seventh is not possible this way.

THE ROUTE THAT DOES ADD OPTIONS is a MelonLoader mod, which this game already runs. Relevant established surface from the brief: CharacterMod carries materialIndex, materialBaseColourReference, ActuallySetMaterial(), ApplyColorModifier(), tattooMaterial, isSkinned/skinnedMesh, and camo variants of one item commonly share a ModName and differ only by material. A mod can therefore inject an extra material into the variant list and set it via ActuallySetMaterial() rather than replacing a file. That path also survives every game patch, because it does not depend on a filename hash.

CAVEAT I HAVE NOT PROVEN: whether the variant list is a fixed-size array read from a ScriptableObject or a runtime List you can append to. That decides whether injection is easy or needs a Harmony patch on the list builder. The probe: MelonLoader hotkey dump enumerating every CharacterMod with ModName, materialIndex, and the length/type of its material collection, per the skill's inventory-dump technique.

SECOND HARD LIMIT: multiplayer. Reskins are client-side presentation. Everyone else sees the stock texture. Nothing about a texture swap crosses the wire, so there is no ban surface and no desync, but also no showing off.

THIRD: Steam. A depot update or 'Verify integrity of game files' without warning restores stock bundles. Ship reskin packs as an installer that copies from a backup folder and re-resolves hashes, not as a one-time manual copy.

findings.reskin: Decide up front: repaint-in-place (easy, N-for-N, breaks on patch) or MelonLoader material injection (harder, additive, patch-proof). Do not start a big pack before choosing.

findings.detail:
Ranked by effort. All bundle names read from the live folder today; re-glob the slug before installing in case the hash has moved.

--- TIER 1, one texture, under an hour, no mip work needed ---

1. ACOG CHEVRON RETICLE RECOLOUR. Bundle weaponmodmaterials_assets_acog_reticle_b99dc4f827ae96acc397f9889952f237.bundle - only 59,252 bytes, the smallest target I found. PAYOFF very high: the reticle fills your screen every time you aim. Best first project in the game.

2. CUSTOM UNIT PATCH. Bundle charactermodmaterials_assets_mi_patch_jtac_f0e978d67142c5381a3e67057da29b62.bundle (2,121,236 B). Textures: 'Patch_JTAC_BaseColor' 1024x1024 DXT1 mips 1 (repaint this), 'Patch_JTAC_Normal' 512 DXT5 mips 10, 'jtac_mask' 512 DXT5 mips 10 (leave both). Addressable .../WSF Operator V2/Textures/PATCHES/PBR_Patch_US_JTAC_tx/MI_Patch_JTAC.mat. 28 patch bundles exist; siblings include mi_patch_3dma_us_co, mi_patch_3dma_us_ir, mi_patch_us_bw, mi_patch_us_bw1, mi_patch_us_ir, mi_patch_us_snake_02, patchgoldensq, patch_3dma_sdr1. PAYOFF high, it is your squad's logo on your shoulder.

3. IR / GLINT PATCH. charactermodmaterials_assets_mi_patch_us_ir_0cd1d0dac4be0e47c8d4c511d63e2a1c.bundle and mi_patch_3dma_us_ir_1b05fefd4e9408357156bc56c513c633.bundle. Same shape as #2. Interesting because these are the NVG-visible variants - a good test of whether the mask texture drives IR response. NEEDS-PROBE: I did not open these two, so I have not confirmed their texture names.

--- TIER 2, one texture but mip-chained, half a day ---

4. SINGLE POUCH CAMO. charactermodmaterials_assets_12x5blk_658479ee2d334e7f96c16dfea7ad1188.bundle. Repaint '12x5 BLK' 2048x2048 DXT1 and you MUST pass mipmap_count=12 or it shimmers. Everything about this one is proven end to end in my round-trip test. PAYOFF moderate, it is one pouch.

5. WEAPON FINISH ON ONE PART. weaponmodmaterials_assets_hk_poly_magazine_39af65da3925f0f5876929db56e78ef0.bundle or ak_mag_akm_std_2eed883b1a26c39e0464419ed8bfc1a6.bundle. Cerakote, battle-worn, tiger stripe. Remember the double-identity trap - pair it with the charactermodmaterials mag if that mag is also worn.

--- TIER 3, families, a weekend ---

6. FULL 12x5 CAMO FAMILY, six bundles. 12x5aor2 / 12x5blk / 12x5gray / 12x5m81 / 12x5mcb / 12x5od. One 2048 texture each, all sharing the same normal and mask. Replace all six with your own six-camo set and it presents as a complete native-looking option list. This is the sweet spot: real deliverable, fully understood pipeline, no new unknowns.

7. FULL RETICLE SET. 95 bundles match retic/eotech/exps/rmr/holo, including 525pm2_reticle, acog_reticle, acrop2_reticle, acrop2_reticlenvg, aimpoint_pro_reticle, aimpoint_pro_reticle1, bravo4_reticle, bravo4_reticle1, burrisreticle. Note the NVG twins (acrop2_reticlenvg, and from catalog_strings 'EXPS2 reticle nvg.mat', 'EXPS3_reticle nvg.mat') - every optic has a night variant you must also do or your reticle changes colour under NVGs. High payoff, mechanical work.

8. WHOLE-KIT CAMO (shirt + trousers + rig + helmet cover) in one new pattern. Discovery step first: grep catalog_strings.txt for the colourway tokens already counted in charactermodmaterials - coyote 40, black 28, mc 28, aor1 25, blk 21, fde 19, tan 14, od 13, m81 6, aor2 4, tigerstripe 3, dts 2. Picking a low-count token like dts (2) or tigerstripe (3) means a tiny complete family; picking coyote (40) means 40 bundles.

--- TIER 4, advanced ---

9. MATCHED MAGAZINE SET ACROSS BOTH WORLDS. All PMAG variants in charactermodmaterials (mi_mag_magpul_pmag_gen3_m3_556_30_blk / _tan / _glass, mi_m4pmagfde, m4pmag_sdr) PLUS the weaponmodmaterials counterparts of 556x4520rndpmag / 556x4540rndpmag / 556x4540rndpmagfde. The hard part is not painting, it is building the join table by eye because the two naming conventions do not share tokens.

10. ADDITIVE CAMO VIA MELONLOADER. Adds options instead of replacing them, survives patches and Steam verify. Requires the CharacterMod inventory-dump probe first (ModName, materialIndex, material collection type and length) to learn whether variants are appendable. Highest payoff, highest risk, and the only route that produces a pack that does not rot.

DEAD/PLACEHOLDER NOTE: I found no obviously dead art in the bundles I opened - all four had complete, coherent texture sets. The only oddity is the misleading OCP token inside the shared normal map name and the shipped typo 'chevon@4x'.

findings.title: Pouches are BAKED geometry, not child sockets — proven by opening a carrier prefab
findings.detail: Opened charactermods_stripped_assets_ferroconceptsfcpcriflemancoyote_3e1ef648aad674c4cecf25280a10fbb5.bundle (3,010,193 bytes) with UnityPy. Object census: 22 GameObject / 22 Transform / 18 MeshRenderer / 18 MeshFilter / 18 Mesh / 5 MonoBehaviour / 1 AssetBundle. Every pouch is a sibling mesh inside the ONE prefab. The only child sockets present are MOD_ArmourPlate and MOD_PatchMain. There is no pouch socket anywhere. Cross-check against the live-game structure already proven in the user's LoadoutPresets work: CharacterCustomisation.modParents contains ONLY named child sockets (Night Vision Mount, Battery Pack, Helmet Cover, FAST MT EarPro, Scrim, V-Lite, Strobe, Armor Plates, Vest Patch Main, Left/Right Arm Patch, Color) and the worn garment itself sits on a direct property (Vest / Belt / Backpack). No 'Pouch' socket exists in either the prefab or the runtime socket list. Consequence: a carrier's pouch layout is fixed at authoring time, which is exactly why the catalog ships one prefab bundle per loadout-variant per colourway (1165 charactermods_stripped bundles). Note also MeshRenderer, NOT SkinnedMeshRenderer — plate carriers are rigid props parented to a bone; CharacterMod.isSkinned/skinnedMesh/skinnedMeshes exist for shirts/pants/gloves, not carriers. Size proof of baking: 'Ferro Concepts FCPC Empty M81' is 233,955 bytes vs 'Rifleman Coyote' 3,010,193 bytes — the pouches ARE the payload.
findings.names: Vest_Ferro_FCPC_V3, Vest_Ferro_FCPC_V3_Cummerbund_L/R, MOD_ArmourPlate, MOD_PatchMain, PistolHolsterHolder (1), SKM_AVS_Zipon

findings.title: Prefabs ship with LoadoutManager.PlaceholderMaterial on every renderer; real materials bind at runtime from a separate Addressable
findings.detail: Read m_Materials off all 18 MeshRenderers of the FCPC Rifleman Coyote prefab: every one of the 24 material slots points to the SAME external reference (m_FileID=2, m_PathID=-5343436609273763532). The bundle's m_Container path is 'Assets/AddressableAssetsStripped/CharacterMods/Ferro Concepts FCPC Rifleman Coyote.prefab' and m_Dependencies is only two CABs — cab-5b00af9b95ebb9aec2086aa927439000 and cab-62081254e5f53c3d16f8fcf3c684729f — and those two CABs are IDENTICAL for the Coyote and the M81 variant. So the colourway material bundle is not a static dependency of the prefab at all. InteropInspector on Assembly-CSharp confirms the mechanism: Il2Cpp.LoadoutManager exposes PlaceholderMaterial (UnityEngine.Material), AllStrippedCharacterMods (AssetReferenceGameObject[]), AllStrippedWeaponMods, and UnloadAddressable(AssetReferenceGameObject, AddressableObjectType, int). Il2Cpp.CharacterMod exposes material (single Material), rendToModify (single Renderer), materialIndex (int), materialBaseColourReference (string), ActuallySetMaterial() which is Private, ApplyColorModifier(), plus isSkinned / isSkinnedisPatch / skinnedMesh / skinnedMeshes. This is why the two bundle families exist and why editing a charactermodmaterials bundle alone is sufficient for a reskin — the prefab bundle never needs touching.
findings.names: LoadoutManager.PlaceholderMaterial, LoadoutManager.AllStrippedCharacterMods, LoadoutManager.UnloadAddressable, AddressableObjectType, CharacterMod.material, CharacterMod.rendToModify, CharacterMod.materialIndex, CharacterMod.materialBaseColourReference, CharacterMod.ActuallySetMaterial (Private)
findings.reskin: Reskin = edit ONLY the charactermodmaterials bundle. Never repack the *_stripped prefab bundle — it contains no real material and repacking it gains nothing. Also: LoadoutManager.CurrentTextureQuality / TextureQualityChanged() / OnTextureQualityIncreased means the game re-runs the texture load on a quality change; a reskin must survive that reload path, so replace the texture inside the bundle rather than patching a live Material at runtime.

findings.title: How a colourway actually works: one prefab bundle PER colourway, and only ONE material per material bundle
findings.detail:
Opened four material bundles. Every single one has the identical shape: 1 Material + 3 Texture2D + 2-3 stripped Shader stubs + 1 AssetBundle object. Never more than one Material. Examples with exact contents:
- charactermodmaterials_assets_mi_vest_lv119_mc_b9a56cf0ac44d3971dbb150e12c971f1.bundle (3,536,070 B): Material 'MI_Vest_LV119_MC'; Texture2D LV119_MC_BaseColor 2048x2048 fmt 10 (DXT1), LV119_OpenGL_Normal 1024x1024 fmt 12 (DXT5), LitMask 512x512 fmt 12.
- charactermodmaterials_assets_vest_ferro_fcpc_coyote_fc4a8c7b8c789813dc1a3f06b5d29b57.bundle (3,495,897 B): Material 'Vest_Ferro_FCPC_Coyote'; Vest_Ferro_FCPC_Coyote_BaseColor 2048x2048 DXT1, Vest_Ferro_FCPC_OCP_DirectX_Normal 1024x1024 DXT5, MaskMap 512x512 DXT5.
- charactermodmaterials_assets_mi_vest_tyr_pico_assaulterspccoyote_04be8897809616c91ceaf2df90b60701.bundle (10,596,537 B): Material 'MI_Vest_TYR_PICO_AssaultersPC Coyote' (note the SPACE before Coyote); all three maps at 2048x2048.
- charactermodmaterials_assets_mi_belt_bison_coyote_14b6be50dd60987e29348f924eeef6fc.bundle (8,973,075 B): Material 'MI_Belt_Bison_Coyote'; BaseMap named 'Bison Belt Coyote_MI_Belt_Bison_Coyote_BaseMap 6', Belt_Bison_MC_tx_Normal, bisonbeltmask, all 2048x2048.
Bound texture properties are HDRP Lit: _BaseColorMap, _NormalMap, _MaskMap (MaskMap = R metallic / G AO / B detail / A smoothness). Older materials additionally alias _MainTex to the same texture as _BaseColorMap.
findings.names: MI_Vest_LV119_MC, Vest_Ferro_FCPC_Coyote, MI_Vest_TYR_PICO_AssaultersPC Coyote, MI_Belt_Bison_Coyote, MI_Pouch_Ferro_GP_6x9_Coyote
findings.reskin: One bundle = one colourway = one material = three textures. Swap the *_BaseColor DXT1 2048 and you have a new camo for that item in that colourway, with zero risk to any other colourway. This is the atomic unit of a reskin project.

findings.title: Two shader generations ship side by side; both stubs are stripped and need Shader.Find
findings.detail:
Materials fall into exactly two groups by shader stub PathID, and the property set differs:
- OLD generation, shader m_PathID 7322088784485553867: MI_Vest_LV119_MC, MI_Belt_Bison_Coyote. 24 _TexEnv entries including _AnisotropyMap, _BentNormalMap, _BentNormalMapOS, _CoatMaskMap, _IridescenceMaskMap, _IridescenceThicknessMap, _SubsurfaceMaskMap, _TangentMap, _ThicknessMap, _TransmissionMaskMap, _TransmittanceColorMap, plus the legacy _MainTex alias. Bundle carries 3 Shader objects.
- NEW generation, shader m_PathID -3661740934848837633: Vest_Ferro_FCPC_Coyote, MI_Vest_TYR_PICO_AssaultersPC Coyote, MI_Pouch_Ferro_GP_6x9_Coyote. Only 8 _TexEnv entries (_BaseColorMap, _DetailMap, _EmissiveColorMap, _MaskMap, _NormalMap + the 3 unity_ lightmap slots), no _MainTex, and it gains _BASE_LAYER_TRIPLANAR, _DETAIL_TRIPLANAR_UV, _ConservativeDepthOffsetEnable floats. Bundle carries 2 Shader objects.
In both cases m_Shader.m_FileID is 0, i.e. it points at the in-bundle stripped Shader stub, which is why bundle materials come back with a dead shader in a modded runtime.
findings.names: _BaseColorMap, _NormalMap, _MaskMap, _MainTex, _BASE_LAYER_TRIPLANAR, _DETAIL_TRIPLANAR_UV, _ConservativeDepthOffsetEnable, _DoubleSidedConstants, _AlphaCutoffEnable
findings.reskin: The shader PathID is a reliable fingerprint for which generation an item belongs to — use it to decide whether your replacement material needs _MainTex populated (old) or not (new). If you load these materials in a mod you still need mat.shader = Shader.Find(mat.shader.name); the stub is inert.

findings.title: THE NORMAL/MASK MAP NAME TRAP: normals are copied across colourways and keep the wrong colour in their name
findings.detail: Proven three times over. The COYOTE FCPC bundle contains a normal map named 'Vest_Ferro_FCPC_OCP_DirectX_Normal'. The COYOTE Ferro GP 6x9 pouch bundle contains 'Pouch_Ferro_GP_6x9_OCP_DirectX_Normal'. The COYOTE Bison belt bundle contains 'Belt_Bison_MC_tx_Normal'. In every case only the BaseColor texture is actually per-colourway ('..._Coyote_BaseColor'); the normal and the mask are the same authored asset duplicated into each colourway bundle, still carrying the name of whichever colourway was authored first (OCP or MC). Separately, normal-map convention is NOT uniform: LV119 ships 'LV119_OpenGL_Normal' (OpenGL, green-up) while the Ferro/FCPC/TYR assets ship '..._DirectX_Normal' (green-down). Mask naming is inconsistent too: 'LitMask', 'MaskMap', 'bisonbeltmask'.
findings.names: Vest_Ferro_FCPC_OCP_DirectX_Normal, Pouch_Ferro_GP_6x9_OCP_DirectX_Normal, Belt_Bison_MC_tx_Normal, LV119_OpenGL_Normal, LitMask, MaskMap, bisonbeltmask
findings.reskin: Never identify which bundle you have open by the texture name — use the bundle filename. Edit BaseColor only unless you deliberately want new surface detail. If you DO replace a normal, check the name for OpenGL vs DirectX and flip the green channel to match, because the game mixes both conventions across items (convention-from-name is inferred, not pixel-verified).

findings.title: Armour plates are gameplay-only items with ZERO art — nothing to reskin
findings.detail: Opened all the plate prefab bundles. charactermods_stripped_assets_ceramicnij4plate_175fb9f75c16d2e998b4567900d61da0.bundle is 3,482 bytes and contains exactly: 1 GameObject ('Ceramic NIJ 4 Plate'), 1 Transform, 2 MonoBehaviour, 1 AssetBundle. No Mesh, no MeshFilter, no MeshRenderer, no Material, no Texture. Same shape for nijiiiasoftarmour (3,475 bytes, container path 'Assets/AddressableAssetsStripped/CharacterMods/NIJ IIIA Soft Armour.prefab', only ONE dependency CAB — the monoscripts one — because it has no renderer). Plates go into the MOD_ArmourPlate child socket (runtime socket name 'Armor Plates'). Their function is the Armour component read in the ballistics path at 0xAF25D1 per OPERATOR_REFERENCE.md line 152: TryGetComponent(out _armour[+0x1C8]); durFrac = durability[+0x30]/maxDurability[+0x2C]; ratingFactor = _ratingFactors[armourRating[+0x28]]; if ratingFactor > armourPenetration[+0x84] roll Random.value > GetPenChance(durFrac) → armourPenetration = 0; plate wear written at 0xAF26EE-0xAF2702; on defeat, damage = round(damage * _bluntDamageMultiplier[+0x134]) taken off the Armour, fragDamage = 0, bleed block skipped.

findings.title: The standalone pouch material catalog — two generations, and this is where per-pouch reskins live

findings.title: Is pouch colour independent of carrier colour? — the definitive answer, with the one probe that remains
findings.detail:
THREE separate levels, and only one of them gives independence.
(1) IN-GAME, NO. The player picks a whole item ('Ferro Concepts FCPC Rifleman Coyote'), and the pouches come with it. CharacterMod exposes ONE materialIndex, ONE material and ONE rendToModify, and the only colour-related socket in the live modParents list is a single 'Color' child socket (CharacterModParent.IsColorModSlot). There is no per-pouch colour control and no pouch socket.
(2) IN THE ART DATA, YES. The carrier prefab has 18 separate MeshRenderers / 24 material slots, and the material catalog carries separately-named, separately-bundled materials whose names match the individual pouch mesh names 1:1. So the data can express a different material per pouch.
(3) FOR A MODDER, YES via bundles. Because a reskin edits the material bundle and the game rebinds materials at runtime, editing mi_pouch_ferro_gp_12x5_coyote changes that pouch wherever it appears, without touching the carrier.
THE REMAINING UNKNOWN: whether ActuallySetMaterial() sprays CharacterMod.material over all child renderers or resolves one material per renderer. CharacterMod.material is singular, which argues for spraying; the existence of per-pouch material bundles argues for per-renderer. The FCPC carrier's own atlas (Vest_Ferro_FCPC_Coyote_BaseColor, 2048x2048) would have to cover shell + 2 cummerbunds + 7 pouches + 4 mags + radio + PTT + folded gloves if it were spraying, which is implausible at that resolution.
findings.names: CharacterMod.material, CharacterMod.rendToModify, CharacterMod.materialIndex, CharacterMod.ActuallySetMaterial (Private), CharacterModParent.IsColorModSlot
findings.reskin: THE PROBE: with MelonLoader, on a spawned 'Ferro Concepts FCPC Rifleman Coyote', walk GetComponentsInChildren<MeshRenderer>() and log renderer.gameObject.name + renderer.material.name for all 18. If you get 18 distinct material names (Vest_Ferro_FCPC_Coyote, MI_Pouch_Ferro_GP_12x5_Coyote, MI_MPU5_Coyote, ...) the per-pouch reskin works. If you get one name repeated 18 times, the whole carrier lives on one atlas and only the whole-carrier reskin is possible. This single log line decides the entire scope of a pouch-level reskin project — run it first.

findings.title: Prefab-to-material colourway parity is broken on most platforms — you cannot assume a material bundle exists per colourway

MSV Gen2 2 vs 2 (clean). Mystery Ranch SATL 16 vs 16 (clean). But: FCPC 36 prefab bundles vs only 3 vest_ferro_fcpc_* materials (aor1/coyote/ocp). TYR PICO 29 prefab bundles vs 2 materials. findings.title: weaponmods_stripped prefabs carry NO material binding — one universal sentinel PPtr for the entire family
findings.detail:
PROVEN by opening 14 prefab bundles with UnityPy 1.25.2 (installed during this pass; it was absent). Every MeshRenderer/SkinnedMeshRenderer in every weapon-attachment prefab I opened points its m_Materials[0] at the identical external pointer (m_FileID=2, m_PathID=-5343436609273763532). Sampled across totally unrelated categories: 556x45pmag, 556x45pmagfde, 556x45pmagwindow, 556x45pmagwindowmcvariant, 556x4540rndpmag, 556x4540rndpmagfde, coltupperreciever, coltupperrecievermcvariant, b5systemsbravostockblkcamo, b5systemsbravostockfde, surefirewarden, magpulrvgfde, eotechexps-3blk, eotechexps-3mcvariant. Global histogram over those bundles: (2, -5343436609273763532) appears 25 times; only TWO other pointers exist in the whole sample, both m_FileID=0 (bundle-internal) and both inside the EOTech EXPS-3 — path_ids 5407560855275626542 and 8341510371973634702, which are the reticle/lens materials that must travel with the optic because they drive a render target.

That is what the '_stripped' in the family name means: Unity's build stripped the material references out of the prefabs and collapsed them to one shared stub. Consequence: the BLK prefab and the FDE prefab of the same part are byte-comparable in their material data — 556x45pmag and 556x45pmagfde are both exactly 266KB with identical mesh sets and identical material pointers. The colour is not in the prefab.

The binding therefore happens at runtime from the attachment definition. identifiers.txt confirms the three helpers exist by exact name: ActuallySetMaterial, ApplyColorModifier, materialIndex. The brief attributes those to CharacterMod; the weapon prefabs exhibit the same stripped-sentinel shape, so the weapon path almost certainly runs through the same or a mirrored helper — that specific call chain is the one thing here I did not disassemble.
findings.names: m_FileID=2 / m_PathID=-5343436609273763532 (sentinel); EOTech-internal fid=0 pid=5407560855275626542, pid=8341510371973634702; ActuallySetMaterial; ApplyColorModifier; materialIndex
findings.reskin: Do not try to reskin by editing a weaponmods_stripped bundle — there is nothing colour-related in it. All finish work happens in weaponmodmaterials. It also explains the 1581-prefab / 1203-material count gap: many prefabs share one material bundle. Corollary for a modder adding a new colourway: cloning the prefab gets you nothing; you must add a material bundle and get the attachment definition to select it (materialIndex).

findings.title: Weapons have NO camo or skin layer. MultiCam is nine hand-authored prefabs, and they compose exactly one rifle.
findings.detail:
This was the open question and the answer is definitive on both sides of the evidence.

CODE SIDE (proven): the string 'Camo' occurs exactly ONCE in the whole IL2CPP identifier table D:\OperatorHSR\re\op\identifiers.txt — line 32804, 'Editor_AddClothingCamos'. Clothing. There is no WeaponSkin, weaponSkin, skinIndex, SkinMaterial, paintJob or camo-anything on the weapon side. No pattern/decal/detail-tiling layer exists to drive.

ART SIDE (proven): searching all 1581 weaponmods_stripped slugs, the only 'camo' tokens are b5systemsbravostockblkcamo and b5systemsbravostockodcamo — and those are two of SEVEN authored colourways of one stock, sitting alongside blk / coyotebrown / fde / grey / odgreen. They are baked-texture SKUs, not a layer.

MultiCam is the closest thing to a pattern and it is 9 prefabs total. Listed as a tree below. Notice what they add up to: Colt upper + Colt lower + DD RIS II handguard + BCM Gunfighter grip (2 orientations) + std AR15 pistol grip + LMT SOPMOD stock + EXPS-3 optic + PMAG Window. That is a complete, buildable MultiCam M4 and nothing else in the game can wear MultiCam. Whoever authored this did one gun and stopped.

The one other real pattern on a weapon is AOR1, and it is on the M79 only: m79barrelsawedoffaor1, m79lockaor1, m79sawedoffbodyaor1, m79triggerguardaor1 (m79safetyswitchfde and m79triggerfde fill the rest). Material side shows mi_gl_m79_devgru_barrel/_body versus mi_gl_m79_devgru_barrelclassic/_bodyclassic — I infer devgru=AOR1 and classic=plain from the pairing, not proven.

So: authored colourways only. The brief's low colourway counts for weaponmodmaterials were an undercount from whole-token matching — substring counts over lines 2240–3442 of bundle_families.json give ~55 FDE material bundles and ~45 blk/black, not 8 and 14. The colourway system is large; it is just not a camo system.

MESH FACTS (proven, read from prefabs). The eight prefabs are not one mesh recoloured — they are three separate art sources:

MATERIAL FACTS (proven, opened each bundle). Shader, texture names, dimensions and formats are real reads, format codes are Unity TextureFormat (10 = DXT1/BC1, 12 = DXT5/BC3):
  • pmag → material 'PMAG', shader HDRP/Lit. _BaseColorMap+_MainTex=Pmag30_low_Pmag30_Diffuse 2048x2048 DXT1; _NormalMap=Pmag30_low_Pmag30_Normal 2048x2048 DXT5; _SpecularColorMap=Pmag30_low_Pmag30_Specular 2048x2048 DXT1; _MaskMap=PMAG_MaskMap 4x4 DXT1.
  • pmag1 → material 'PMAG 1', shader HDRP/Lit. Same normal/specular/4x4 mask, but _BaseColorMap=Pmag30_Base_Color 2048x2048 DXT1. So PMAG vs PMAG 1 differ by base colour ONLY.
  • pmag_40 → 'PMAG_40', HDRP/Lit, _BaseColorMap=BLK_PMAG40_low_PMAG_40_BaseColor 512x512 DXT1, _NormalMap=PMAG40_low_PMAG_40_Normal 1024x1024 DXT5, _MaskMap=PMAG40_low_PMAG_40_MaskMap 512x512 DXT5.
  • pmag_40fde → 'PMAG_40 FDE', identical normal + mask, _BaseColorMap=FDE_PMAG40_low_PMAG_40_BaseColor 512x512 DXT1. Textbook one-texture colourway.
  • magmc → 'mag mc', shader MilkShaders/Lit-Template. _BaseColorMap='pmag_m3_BaseColor mc' 2048x2048 DXT1, _MaskMap=pmag_m3_OcclusionRoughnessMetallic 512x512 DXT5, _NormalMap=pmag_m3_Normal 1024x1024 DXT5. No _MainTex.
  • magfde → 'mag fde', same MilkShaders/Lit-Template, same normal + ORM, _BaseColorMap=pmag_m3_BaseColor 512x512 DXT1.
  • mag_glass → 'mag_Glass', HDRP/Lit, ZERO textures. The window insert is pure shader parameters.

The magmc/magfde pair is the money shot: MultiCam on the PMAG was authored by swapping one map, pmag_m3_BaseColor 512 -> 'pmag_m3_BaseColor mc' 2048, on the same shader with the same normal and ORM.

Which prefab binds which material is NOT recoverable from the prefabs (see the sentinel finding); the tree below marks bindings I infer from mesh/texture correspondence. Resolving it exactly needs a runtime probe: spawn each attachment and log renderer.sharedMaterial.name.

findings.title: The two-worlds PMAG trap, proven down to texture names and resolutions
findings.detail:
The brief warned about this; here it is with hard evidence, which also shows it is worse than 'different materials' — the two worlds use entirely different TEXTURES at different resolutions, so there is no shared file to edit even by accident.

WEAPON world (magazine in the gun): weaponmodmaterials_assets_pmag_4efa1c6f9ce988751fd2139336d6f3c6.bundle → material 'PMAG' → base colour 'Pmag30_low_Pmag30_Diffuse', 2048x2048 DXT1, normal 'Pmag30_low_Pmag30_Normal' 2048x2048.

CHARACTER world (magazine in the chest rig): charactermodmaterials_assets_mi_pmag_556_e6388d7446e5ff293e3a55fcdeea5258.bundle → material 'MI_PMAG_556', shader HDRP/Lit → base colour 'PMAG_Black_BaseColor', 1024x1024 DXT1, normal 'PMAG_Black_Normal' 1024x1024, mask 'MI_PMAG_556_MaskMap' 2048x2048 DXT1.

Different material name, different texture names, different resolutions, different mask sizes. Editing Pmag30_low_Pmag30_Diffuse changes the loaded magazine and leaves every pouch magazine untouched, and vice versa.

The character world carries SIX PMAG material bundles that must all be handled to fully repaint pouch mags: m4pmag_sdr, mi_m4pmagfde, mi_mag_magpul_pmag_gen3_m3_556_30_blk, …_556_30_tan, …_m3_glass, mi_pmag_556 (display names from catalog: 'M4Pmag_sdr.mat', 'MI_M4Pmag FDE.mat', 'MI_Mag_Magpul_PMAG_GEN3_M3_556_30_BLK.mat', '…_Tan.mat', '…_Glass.mat', 'MI_PMAG_556.mat').

Note also that BOTH worlds ship a 'PMAG GEN3 M3' magazine — weaponmodmaterials has magazine_pmag30_genm3 / genm31 / genm32 while charactermodmaterials has mi_mag_magpul_pmag_gen3_m3_556_30_blk / _tan. Same real-world product, two independent art pipelines, and the weapon side has THREE same-named copies.

findings.title: Shader reality check: weapon materials are HDRP/Lit or MilkShaders/Lit-Template, and the vendor shader names in the catalog are DEAD strings
findings.detail:
Two corrections to assumptions a reskinner would otherwise make.

1. catalog_strings.txt contains what look like per-vendor shaders: 'ParallaxGameStudios/PMAG' (15650), 'ParallaxGameStudios/STANAG' (15651), 'ParallaxGameStudios/I5AWM' (15649), 'Magpul/Pmag30' (14858), 'Magpul/afg' (14859), 'PMAG40/HDRP' (15631). These are NOT in use. PROVEN: I byte-scanned every file in D:\Games\OPERATOR\OPERATOR_Data — the tokens 'ParallaxGameStudios', 'Magpul/' and 'PMAG40' occur ZERO times anywhere in the shipped player data (globalgamemanagers, globalgamemanagers.assets, resources.assets, level0-level30, all sharedassets). And when I opened the actual pmag/pmag1/pmag_40/pmag_40fde bundles, the Shader objects inside are HDRP/Lit, Hidden/HDRP/FallbackError, Hidden/Core/FallbackError. The vendor names are leftover source-pack strings that survived into the catalog string table; the materials were re-targeted to HDRP/Lit at import. Do not write Shader.Find("ParallaxGameStudios/PMAG") — it returns null and you get magenta.

2. Weapon materials split across exactly two shader families, and the split is per-vendor-pack, not per-part:
   • HDRP/Lit — pmag, pmag1, pmag_40, pmag_40fde, mag_glass, magblk, and (character side) mi_pmag_556. Property set: _BaseColorMap, _MainTex (aliased to the same texture), _MaskMap, _NormalMap, and sometimes _SpecularColorMap.
   • MilkShaders/Lit-Template — magmc, magfde. Property set: _BaseColorMap, _MaskMap (an OcclusionRoughnessMetallic pack), _NormalMap. NO _MainTex, NO _SpecularColorMap. Fallback stub in-bundle is Hidden/Shader Graph/FallbackError, confirming it is a Shader Graph asset.

Both resolve safely via Shader.Find. PROVEN from globalgamemanagers' always-included shader list: 'HDRP/Lit' is present, and the MilkShaders family ships in full — MilkShaders/Lit-Rocks, /Lit-Template, /Lit-Template-AddLayer, /Lit-Template-AddLayer-Tess, /Lit-Template-AddTwoLayer, /Lit-Template-POM, /Lit-Template-Tess, /Lit-Template-Triplanar, /OLD/Lit-Triplanar-Tess, /OLD/OLD-PBR-Triplanar, /OLD/PBR-Triplanar-Tess, /UERemap, /UERemapDecal, /UERemapDecalPOM, /UERemapTriplaner, /WhiteBoard (16 entries).

The stripping is real but survivable: each material bundle carries a name-only shader stub plus the FallbackError shaders, which is exactly the documented broken-ref condition. The fix mat.shader = Shader.Find(mat.shader.name) works here because the surviving names ('HDRP/Lit', 'MilkShaders/Lit-Template') are both in the shipped registry.

findings.reskin: Author against HDRP/Lit conventions (BaseColor + BC5-style normal + HDRP MaskMap = R metallic / G AO / B detail / A smoothness). For the MilkShaders parts remember _MaskMap is an OcclusionRoughnessMetallic pack, i.e. a DIFFERENT channel order from HDRP's — get this backwards and the magazine goes chrome or dead matte. Always set _BaseColorMap and _MainTex together on the HDRP/Lit materials; the game writes both and code that reads _MainTex will otherwise see the old texture.

findings.title: Attachment-category tree of weaponmodmaterials, with which finishes actually ship per category
findings.detail:
Built by classifying all 1203 slugs at lines 2240-3442 of D:\OperatorHSR\re\op\bundle_families.json, cross-read against the 1581 prefab slugs at 3445-5025. Category assignment is from naming (inferred); the slug names themselves are proven.

The finish vocabulary is bigger than the brief's token counts suggested. Real substring counts over the material family: FDE ~55 bundles, BLK/BLACK ~45, plus GRY/GREY/GRAY, OD/ODG/ODGRN/ODGREEN/OLIVE, TAN/COYOTETAN/SAND, GRN/GREEN, MC ~6, and a long one-off tail (GOLD/GOLDEN/GLD, RED, WHITE, PINK, SILVER, BRONZE, CHAMELEON, TIN, STAINLESS, STEEL, PIT).

The important structural fact is that finish depth varies enormously by category, and it maps to how visible the part is:
  • BARRELS use a different axis entirely — not BLK/FDE but BLK vs STEEL (nitride vs stainless), and they draw on the generic shared materials black/black1/black2 and steel/steel1/steel2 rather than per-barrel materials. 30+ AR barrel prefabs, 2 finishes each, ~6 material bundles total.
  • BIPODS are the thinnest category in the game: ONE material bundle (bipod_cvlife-6-9inches-mlok) plus spr300_bipod. Zero colourways. Prefabs are deployed/folded state, not finish.
  • HANDGUARDS/RAILS are the deepest: KAC URX4 ships every length in three finishes (blk/fde/tan), SIG Virtus ships four lengths x SD/non-SD x three finishes (blk/gray/fde) = 18 prefabs.
  • PISTOL SLIDES carry the exotic finishes — the L2D/Zaffari/ZEV Glock ecosystem is where bronze/chameleon/tin/stainless live, and the TTI Pit Viper adds pink/silver.
  • OPTICS are mostly BLK/FDE plus a reticle/glass sub-layer that is NOT a finish (see traps).

findings.reskin: Pick a branch by finish depth. Cheapest high-impact project: the shared generic materials — black, blk, steel, gripblk/gripfde/gripmc, magblk/magfde/magmc, buttblk/buttfde — because a handful of bundles repaint dozens of prefabs at once. Most expensive: handguards, where every length is its own material bundle. If the goal is one coherent camouflaged rifle, follow the MultiCam 9-bundle template rather than trying to cover a category.

findings.title: Dead assets, placeholder art and five naming traps that will make you edit the wrong bundle
findings.detail:
All PROVEN from the slug list or from opened bundles.

DEAD / PLACEHOLDER MATERIALS in weaponmodmaterials:
  • modplaceholdermaterial — self-declaring placeholder, still shipped.
  • newmaterial, newmaterial1, newmaterial2, newmaterial3, newmaterial4 — five untouched Unity default names.
  • default1 — Unity default.
  • Single-letter / meaningless: 'b', '_low', 'low', 'low1', 'large01', 'large011', 'large012', 'large013', 'b30b31c', 'efr', 'maid', 'maid1', 'white', 'glass', 'steel', 'steel1', 'steel2', 'extension', 'extension1', 'extension2', 'extension3'. Each is its own shipped bundle.
  • Non-attachment strays sitting in the weapon-finish family: muzzleflash1/2/4/5 (note the missing 3), muzzleparticles, smoke, flame1, flame2, distortion, 919_bullet, 919_case, primer_new_silver, bolt.

PLACEHOLDER TEXTURE (proven by opening the bundle): PMAG_MaskMap is 4x4 pixels, DXT1, and is bound to _MaskMap on BOTH the PMAG and PMAG 1 materials. A 4x4 mask is a flat constant — the PMAG has no working metallic/AO/smoothness map at all. Anyone authoring a proper HDRP MaskMap for it is adding detail the shipped asset never had.

TRAP 1 — the numeric-suffix duplicates. Addressables disambiguates same-named materials by appending 1, 2, 11, 21. handguard_10, handguard_101 and handguard_1011 are THREE separate bundles that all contain a material named 'Handguard_10'. Same for rail_ar_mk4_7 / _71 / _72 / _721, exps3 / 31 / 32 / 321 / 33, and dozens more. You cannot tell from the name which one a given attachment consumes. Resolving it requires a runtime probe: log renderer.sharedMaterial and the loaded bundle for the specific attachment.

TRAP 2 — magBLK is not a generic magazine. Opened it: material 'magBLK' but its textures are SCAR-H_magazine_20_BLACK_AlbedoTransparency and SCAR-H_magazine_20_BLACK_Normal (512, DXT1/DXT5) plus magBLK_MaskMap 512. It is the SCAR-H 20rnd mag. Its sibling magfde is a PMAG (pmag_m3_*). Same name stem, unrelated parts.

TRAP 3 — '556x45 20rnd PMAG' contains no PMAG mesh. Proven: the prefab's meshes are SM_AACHB_01a_mag and SM_AACHB_01a_mag_follower.

TRAP 4 — optic 'finish' bundles that are not finishes. Every *_reticle, *_reticlenvg, *_rearglass, *_frontglass, *_lens, *_rendertarget, plus scopeeffect / scopeeffectndr / distortion, are optical-path materials. These are the only weapon materials that survive inside prefab bundles (fid=0 pointers in the EXPS-3). Editing them changes the sight picture, not the housing colour, and breaking one breaks aiming.

TRAP 5 — bundle content hashes. The filename hash trap did NOT bite on this family: I Glob'd the live folder and all 33 PMAG bundles match the hashes recorded in catalog_strings.txt. But that is a snapshot. Re-scan and rename to the CURRENT on-disk hash after every patch.

One actually interesting orphan: 'railskins' and 'railcovers' both exist as materials (and railcovers/dd_railcovers as prefabs). 'railskins' is the only asset in the whole weapon family whose name implies a skin concept, and it is a rail-cover material — not evidence of a skin system.
findings.names: modplaceholdermaterial; newmaterial/1/2/3/4; default1; PMAG_MaskMap (4x4 DXT1); magBLK -> SCAR-H_magazine_20_BLACK_AlbedoTransparency; SM_AACHB_01a_mag; railskins; railcovers; handguard_10/101/1011; rail_ar_mk4_7/71/72/721
findings.reskin: Before editing any bundle whose slug ends in a bare digit, prove the mapping with a runtime probe — a MelonLoader patch that dumps, per spawned attachment, the GameObject name, renderer.sharedMaterial.name and the owning bundle. That single probe converts most of the 'inferred' bindings in this report to proven and is the highest-value next step for any reskin project. Skip modplaceholdermaterial, newmaterial*, default1 and the muzzleflash/particle strays entirely.

findings.title: Verdict: world, VFX and UI art are NOT addressable — only 6 VFX materials and 1 prop material ship in bundles
findings.detail: PROVEN by enumerating the live folder (Glob, 4,989 .bundle + 1 stray file) and grepping D:\OperatorHSR\re\op\catalog_strings.txt. Outside the four art families there are exactly four bundles: `5df1b7680c9342147f466a5ca660184a_unitybuiltinassets_fae0c879bbeef66081109276ec60eb69.bundle` (1 Material `Sprites-Default` / shader `Sprites/Default`, 19 KB), `5df1b7680c9342147f466a5ca660184a_monoscripts_8f1fa9a40d2b384c5aa93daaa359076e.bundle` (69 MonoScript, 5 KB), `defaultlocalgroup_assets_mat_carryhandle_2034f6e90a7a07d4d2906186afbee036.bundle` (9.24 MB), plus 12 localization bundles. The catalog contains ZERO entries matching terrain, vegetation, prop, building, skybox, decal, icon, sprite or scene asset names — I grepped for all of them and got only weapon/character mod hits. `UnityEngine.ResourceManagement.ResourceProviders.SceneProvider` is registered in the catalog but no scene is addressable. Consequence: a world/VFX/UI reskin is NOT a bundle-swap project like the GIGN charactermodmaterials pack. It is a `.assets`/`level*` file-surgery project (UABEA / AssetsTools.NET) or a runtime MelonLoader material/sprite injection project.
findings.names: unitybuiltinassets, monoscripts, defaultlocalgroup_assets_mat_carryhandle, Sprites-Default, Sprites/Default
findings.reskin: Decide the route first. Addressable bundle-replacement (the proven, safe technique) reaches only the 6 VFX materials in finding 3. Everything else in this area needs either UABEA on OPERATOR_Data\*.assets / level* (offline, breaks on patch) or a MelonLoader mod that walks live objects and swaps Material/Sprite at runtime (patch-durable).

findings.title: The 6 addressable VFX bundles — exact textures, formats and shaders (this is the whole moddable VFX surface)
findings.detail:
PROVEN by opening each bundle with UnityPy 1.25.2 (FALLBACK_UNITY_VERSION="6000.3.8f1"). Every one is a 4-object bundle: 1 Texture2D + 1 Material + 1 stripped Shader stub + 1 AssetBundle. Format code 12 = DXT5/BC3 throughout.
  muzzleflash1 (45,488 B): TEX `MuzzleFlash1` 256x256 DXT5 9 mips -> MAT `MuzzleFlash1`, shader `KriptoFX/FPS_Pack/Particles`, _MainTex
  muzzleflash2 (152,754 B): TEX `Flame1` 512x512 DXT5 10 mips -> MAT `MuzzleFlash2`, same shader
  muzzleflash4 (70,274 B): TEX `MuzzleFlash3` 256x256 DXT5 9 mips -> MAT `MuzzleFlash4`
  muzzleflash5 (44,844 B): TEX `MuzzleFlash4` 256x128 DXT5 9 mips -> MAT `MuzzleFlash5`
  muzzleparticles (20,038 B): TEX `Particle` 32x32 DXT5 1 mip -> MAT `MuzzleParticles`, shader `KriptoFX/FPS_Pack/GlowAdditiveNoFade`
  smoke (467,591 B): TEX `Smoke` 2048x2048 DXT5 12 mips -> MAT `Smoke`, shader `KriptoFX/FPS_Pack/AlphaBlendedAnim` (flipbook)
TRAP: the texture name is offset from the material name. `MuzzleFlash4.mat` uses a texture called `MuzzleFlash3`; `MuzzleFlash5.mat` uses `MuzzleFlash4`; `MuzzleFlash2.mat` uses `Flame1`. Search by bundle slug, never by texture name. TRAP 2: there is no muzzleflash3 bundle at all — the numbering 1,2,4,5 has a real hole, so do not assume a missing file means a bad scan.
findings.names: MuzzleFlash1, Flame1, MuzzleFlash3, MuzzleFlash4, Particle, Smoke, KriptoFX/FPS_Pack/Particles, KriptoFX/FPS_Pack/GlowAdditiveNoFade, KriptoFX/FPS_Pack/AlphaBlendedAnim
findings.reskin: These 6 are the only VFX assets a modder can reskin with the proven bundle-replacement workflow. Replace the DXT5 texture inside the bundle, keep the object name and mip count, rename the file to the CURRENT 32-hex hash from a live re-scan. Repainting `Smoke` (2048x2048 flipbook) changes every muzzle smoke puff in the game; repainting `Particle` (32x32) changes all additive muzzle sparks. All three KriptoFX shaders are in the globalgamemanagers registry, so `Shader.Find` rebinding works with those exact strings.

findings.title: Full shader registry: 351 shaders in globalgamemanagers.assets, not ~180 — with the complete world/VFX/UI family tree
findings.detail: PROVEN by UnityPy-reading every Shader object in D:\Games\OPERATOR\OPERATOR_Data\globalgamemanagers.assets and taking m_ParsedForm.m_Name. Count is 351, of which 214 are `Hidden/*` engine/HDRP internals — the existing OPERATOR_REFERENCE.md figure of "roughly 180 in twelve families" undercounts by ~2x and misses several vendor families. Corrections to the reference doc: it says AmplifyImpostors has "no shaders" — but six impostor shaders DO ship (`Shader Graphs/Book Of The Dead HemiOctahedral Impostor`, `Lit Hemi Octahedral Impostor`, `Lit Octahedral Impostor`, `BotD_Graph_Lit`, `BotD_Graph_Lit_TranslucentAlphaCutoff`, `BotD_Graph_Lit_TranslucentAlphaCutoff_GRASS`). It also does not mention Hovl or Vefects, both of which are present as shaders. `Sprites/Default` is NOT in this registry — it lives only inside the unitybuiltinassets bundle, so `Shader.Find("Sprites/Default")` for a runtime UI material may return null.

findings.title: The prefab->material binding is an Addressables GUID, not a bundle filename — proven from a real prefab
findings.detail: PROVEN. The SECOND MonoBehaviour on `charactermods_stripped_assets_airbosslbmgasmask_...bundle` has exactly two payload keys: `m_Name` and `AllMaterialReferences`. Its value is `[{'Renderer': {'m_FileID':0,'m_PathID':-4879292080498470720}, 'Materials': [{'m_AssetGUID':'9864b206a4e51074d8429e8dcf6ab2ee','m_SubObjectName':'','m_SubObjectType':''}]}]`. So each renderer is paired with an `AssetReference` carrying a 32-hex asset GUID that Addressables resolves to a charactermodmaterials bundle at load time. Separately, on the same prefab the older binding path is dead: `material`, `baseColour` and `tattooMaterial` are all `{m_FileID:0, m_PathID:0}` (null), `materialIndex`=0, `modifyColour`=0, `textureModifer`=0.

findings.reskin: This is why bundle-content replacement works and bundle-ADDITION does not. Editing the texture inside an existing material bundle keeps the GUID intact, so the prefab still resolves. Shipping a brand-new material bundle requires its GUID to be registered in catalog.bin, which the filename-hash rename trick does not do. For world/VFX/UI there is no equivalent GUID indirection at all — those materials are direct m_PathID references inside level*/sharedassets*.

findings.title: Vegetation and most props have no GameObject and no Renderer — the single biggest world-reskin trap
findings.detail: READ from D:\OperatorHSR\re\op\OPERATOR_REFERENCE.md line 89, and corroborated by metadata: `Il2CppBRGInstancedRenderer` types exist (`BRGRenderer`, `BRGRegisterer`, `PrototypeData`, `InstanceData`, `InstanceLink`, `CellContext`, `BRGMeshLodData`, `BRGLightProbes`, `RangeAllocator`). Vegetation and props are drawn through `BatchRendererGroup` with its own GPU HZB occlusion culling: these objects have NO GameObject and NO Renderer, so `FindObjectsOfType`, renderer raycasts and `renderer.material` swaps all without warning miss them. `NakedTerrainRenderer` sets `drawTreesAndFoliage = false`. Yet level16/17 each carry 60,174 real `Tree` objects in the TerrainData tree instance list — so the two systems coexist: terrain-painted trees in Tree instances, everything else through BRG.
findings.names: BRGInstancedRenderer.BRGRenderer, BRGRegisterer, PrototypeData, BRGMeshLodData, NakedTerrainRenderer, drawTreesAndFoliage
findings.reskin: A runtime foliage/prop reskin mod that iterates renderers will appear to do nothing and the modder will assume their patch never bound. The only runtime handle is `BRGInstancedRenderer.PrototypeData` — the material lives on the prototype, not on any scene object. Offline editing of the Material inside the owning sharedassetsN.assets is the reliable route for BRG-drawn art. This must be stated up front in any world-reskin guide.

Everything else named `ReflectionProbe-N` is a BAKED per-scene probe — sharedassets20 and sharedassets24 alone carry 180 and 178 of them, sharedassets22/29 138 each. IES light-cookie cubemaps are scattered: `AreaLight-Cube-IES` (sa2), `Bollard-Cube-IES` / `XArrow-Cube-IES` (sa3), `TopPost-Cube-IES` (sa4), `DO2RD40AS830NW-Cube-IES` (sa5), `ThreeLobeUmbrella-Cube-IES` (sa23), `XArrowSoft-Cube-IES` (sa1). Sky shaders available: `Skybox/Cubemap`, `Skybox/Procedural`, `HDRP/PhysicallyBasedSky`, `HDRPSamples/NightSky_ToCubemaptarget`. Baked GI lives outside all of this: `OPERATOR_Data\StreamingAssets\APVStreamingAssets\` holds 11 GUID-named Adaptive Probe Volume baking sets (~3 .bytes cells each).
findings.names: DefaultHDRISky, starmap_2020_4k, Simple_Cubemap, modern, Interior_A_Day 1, ReflectionProbe-N, APVStreamingAssets
findings.reskin: A sky reskin is tractable and high-impact: replace `DefaultHDRISky` in globalgamemanagers.assets (global) or `starmap_2020_4k` in sharedassets0 (night maps only). The hard limit: reflection probes and the 11 APV sets are BAKED. Any terrain or architecture retexture will leave lighting and reflections referencing the OLD albedo, and there is no way to rebake without the project. Plan reskins that preserve overall luminance, or the mismatch shows on every wall.

findings.title: Impact/decal/blood VFX are pooled prefabs in scenes, budget-divided at boot — reachable at runtime, not by bundle
findings.detail: Partly READ from OPERATOR_REFERENCE.md, partly proven from metadata and the scene census. `PoolInitializer.InitPools` divides one global `TotalDecalBudget`/`TotalVFXBudget` across every registered `SurfaceInformation` prefab, so adding a surface shrinks every other pool toward `MinDecalsPerPrefab`. `BulletInstance.SpawnImpactNewSystem` frustum-culls via `Camera.WorldToViewportPoint` then rate-limits through `BulletEffectManager.CanSpawnImpactVFX` / `MaxImpactVFXPerFrame`, spawning through `ObjectPooler.InstantiatePooled`. The metadata note is explicit that the budget is "split across all VFX prefabs so total concurrent impact VFX stays bounded no matter how many VFX prefabs exist". Blood is `Knife\Real Blood` (DecalProjectorTester) plus `KriptoFX\VolumetricBloodFX` (BFX_BloodSettings, BFX_DecalSettings, BFX_ShaderProperies [sic], BFX_BloodDecalLayers, BFX_RenderDepth, BFX_ManualAnimationUpdate) with shaders `Shader Graphs/BFX_Decal` and `Shader Graphs/BloodDecal HDRP`. Per-scene ParticleSystem counts I measured: level3 31, level6 30, level7 30, level16 18, level19 39, level20 40, level22 36, level24 46, level27/28 18, level21/23 12, level26 5.
findings.names: PoolInitializer, TotalDecalBudget, TotalVFXBudget, MinDecalsPerPrefab, BulletEffectManager.CanSpawnImpactVFX, MaxImpactVFXPerFrame, SurfaceInformation, BFX_BloodSettings, Shader Graphs/BFX_Decal, PooledImpactDecal.placed, RemoveAllDecals
findings.reskin: An impact/blood VFX reskin is a RUNTIME job, not a file job: after `ShaderWarmup.IsComplete`, walk the ObjectPooler's pooled decal/VFX prefabs and swap the Material or its `_MainTex`. Never `Object.Destroy` anything carrying a `PooledObject`. The per-scene ParticleSystem counts above are small (5-46), so enumerating them in a loaded scene is cheap. NEEDS PROBE: I did not read the actual decal/VFX prefab names or their material names — they live in level*/sharedassets* and would need either a runtime `FindObjectsOfTypeAll<SurfaceInformation>()` dump or a full UABEA walk of one map's sharedassets.
