findings.reskin: Any replacement you author must land as DXT1 for colour and DXT5 for normal/mask, at 2048 or 1024, with a full mip chain and streaming enabled, or it will not match its neighbours. Authoring a BC7 replacement is fine visually but doubles the byte size of that texture and changes the bundle footprint.

findings.title: Normal maps are AG-swizzled DXT5nm: R is dead (255), X lives in ALPHA, Y in GREEN, B duplicates G
findings.detail:
Decoded pixels, not inferred. Per-channel means over a 64x64 resample (0-1 scale, with raw min/max):
  Delta_MC_Normal        R=1.000 (255,255)  G=0.493 (2,216)  B=0.494 (4,216)  A=0.496 (28,210)
  Miscellaneous_Normal   R=1.000 (255,255)  G=0.491 (7,235)  B=0.492 (7,235)  A=0.499 (25,239)
  T_Pouches_N            R=1.000 (255,255)  G=0.495 (60,166) B=0.495 (62,165) A=0.499 (65,177)

R is a hard constant 255 in every normal sampled. G and B are bit-identical (same min, same max, same mean) - the DXT1 colour block is encoding ONE channel and replicating it. A carries a second, independent 0.5-centred signal.

That is the DXT5nm / AG layout Unity produces from the 'Normal map' import type on DirectX: X in alpha, Y in green, R forced to 1 as the detection flag. HDRP's UnpackNormalmapRGorAG multiplies x by w, so R=1 means 'take X from A'. The B channel is wasted storage.

All materials that bind a normal carry the keyword _NORMALMAP_TANGENT_SPACE (and _NORMALMAP when the slot is filled), confirming tangent space, not object space. _NormalScale is 1.0 on every material I read.
findings.names: Delta_MC_Normal, Miscellaneous_Normal, T_Pouches_N, _NormalMap, _NORMALMAP_TANGENT_SPACE, _NormalScale
findings.reskin: If you author a normal map as a plain RGB tangent normal and inject it as DXT5 without Unity's normal-map import, R will be your X channel instead of 255, UnpackNormalmapRGorAG will multiply X by your alpha, and the surface will light wrong (usually flat or inverted on one axis). Replacement normals MUST be re-encoded to DXT5nm - i.e. import as Normal Map in a Unity project and re-export, or hand-pack (255, Y, Y, X).

findings.title: MaskMap channel order confirmed by pixel probe: R=Metallic, G=AO, B=Detail, A=Smoothness (standard HDRP) - but one big sub-population is packed differently
findings.detail:
_MaskMap is the dominant PBR slot: 2,003 bindings, third only to _NormalMap (2,076) and _BaseColorMap (2,058).

Probe A - textbook HDRP packing, PROVEN:
  'MaskMap' in charactermodmaterials/mi_mag_magpul_pmag_gen3_m3_556_30_blk (MilkShaders/Lit-Template)
     R=0.010 (metallic ~0 - correct, polymer)  G=0.742 (AO)  B=1.000 constant (detail mask)  A=0.361 (smoothness, matte polymer)
  'MI_PMAG_556_MaskMap' in charactermodmaterials/mi_pmag_556 (HDRP/Lit, keyword _MASKMAP)
     R=0.020  G=0.642  B=1.000 constant  A=forced 1.0 (DXT1, see the DXT1-maskmap finding)

Probe B - a DIFFERENT packing under the same slot name:
  'watch_low_hands_MaskMap' in charactermodmaterials/hands (HDRP/Lit, keyword _MASKMAP)
     R=0.968 (0,255)  G=0.636  B=0.000 constant  A=0.736
  R near-white on a hands/watch material cannot be metallic. This reads as R=AO, B=0 detail. So at least some 'MaskMap'-named textures are authored with AO in R rather than metallic.

Slot-level float defaults are uniform across almost every material read: _AORemapMin 0 / _AORemapMax 1, _SmoothnessRemapMin 0 / _SmoothnessRemapMax 1, _Metallic 0, _Smoothness 0.5, _UVDetail 0, _DetailAlbedoScale/_DetailNormalScale/_DetailSmoothnessScale all 1, _DiffusionProfileHash 0 (except M_Head = 3.215), _SurfaceType 0 (opaque).
findings.names: _MaskMap, _MASKMAP, MaskMap, MI_PMAG_556_MaskMap, watch_low_hands_MaskMap, _AORemapMin/Max, _SmoothnessRemapMin/Max
findings.tree:
_MaskMap RGBA (HDRP convention, confirmed on MilkShaders/Lit-Template + HDRP/Lit)
├── R  Metallic          (~0 on polymer, ~1 on steel)
├── G  Ambient Occlusion (0.6-0.8 typical)
├── B  Detail mask       (constant 255 or constant 0 - never authored)
└── A  Smoothness        (the ONLY channel that survives DXT5; lost under DXT1)

exception population
└── 'watch_low_hands_MaskMap' style: R=AO, B=0  -> re-check any hand/skin mask before editing R
findings.reskin: For a repack you edit A for gloss and R for metal. B is free real estate and is ignored (no material in the game sets _UVDetail non-zero or binds a _DetailMap except 6 outliers). Before editing R on any character-skin or glove mask, sample it: if the mean is >0.9 it is an AO map wearing a MaskMap name and editing it as metallic will chrome the model.

findings.title: Four texture-naming dialects coexist; 'MilkShaders/UERemap' is the developer's Unreal-ORM adapter shader
findings.detail:
The art is bought from multiple vendors and each vendor's export preset survived intact. I cross-tabulated every material's bound slot against the bound texture's name suffix across all 2,601 materials.

_MaskMap is fed by: MaskMap 1,005 | Mask 549 | OcclusionRoughnessMetallic 282 | ORM 21 | other 146
_BaseColorMap is fed by: BaseColor 677 | BaseMap 373 | AlbedoTransparency 235 | Albedo 52 | *_D 41 | other 661
_NormalMap: Normal 1,857 | *_N 58 | other 154
_SpecularColorMap (200 bindings): SpecularSmoothness 184
_SpecGlossMap (113): *_Roughness 113
_MetallicGlossMap (114): *_Metallic 38

The decisive cross-tab: MilkShaders/UERemap has 207 materials and 207 of its _MaskMap bindings are ORM-named (197 *_OcclusionRoughnessMetallic + 10 *_ORM). Not one is a real MaskMap. That is a 100% correlation - UERemap is a shader written specifically to consume Unreal Engine ORM packs (R=AO, G=Roughness, B=Metallic) and remap them into HDRP's (R=Metallic, G=AO, B=Detail, A=Smoothness) at sample time.

Separately, 76 textures are named *_MaskMap_AutodeskToHDRP (all BC7). These are machine-generated by Unity's Autodesk-Interactive-to-HDRP material upgrader, which bakes a proper packed mask from the legacy Autodesk inputs. Examples: ANPRC152_sdr_MaskMap_AutodeskToHDRP, MI_Balaclava_WH_MaskMap_AutodeskToHDRP, Comtac_4_Headset_MaskMap_AutodeskToHDRP, G17_sdr_MaskMap_AutodeskToHDRP, MI_Belt_TYR_MaskMap_AutodeskToHDRP. 116 materials still run HDRP/Autodesk Interactive/AutodeskInteractive.
findings.names: MilkShaders/UERemap, MilkShaders/Lit-Template, HDRP/Autodesk Interactive/AutodeskInteractive, *_MaskMap_AutodeskToHDRP, *_OcclusionRoughnessMetallic, *_SpecularSmoothness
findings.tree:
naming dialect -> where it came from -> which slot it lands in
├── HDRP native      *_BaseColor / *_Normal / *_MaskMap
│     -> HDRP/Lit, MilkShaders/Lit-Template   (the majority)
├── Unreal / Quixel  *_AlbedoTransparency / *_Normal / *_OcclusionRoughnessMetallic (or *_ORM)
│     -> MilkShaders/UERemap (207 mats, remaps correctly)
│     -> LEAKED into MilkShaders/Lit-Template (91) + HDRP/Lit (14) + unresolved (11)
├── Unity Standard-Specular  *_AlbedoTransparency / *_SpecularSmoothness
│     -> _SpecularColorMap (200) on HDRP/Autodesk Interactive
├── URP-ish          *_BaseMap / *_MaskMap
└── vendor shorthand T_<Part>_D / _N / _E / _ORM  (the character-body set: T_Head_D, T_Eye_N, T_Headgears_E, T_Glove5_ORM)
findings.reskin: The suffix tells you the packing, and the packing tells you which channel to paint. Before touching any *_OcclusionRoughnessMetallic, check the material's shader: under UERemap you edit UE ordering (AO,Rough,Metal); under Lit-Template/HDRP-Lit the same file is being read as HDRP ordering and your edits will land in the wrong channels.

findings.title: 116 materials feed an Unreal ORM into a shader that does NOT remap - wrong channels shipped
findings.detail:
Materials that bind an *_OcclusionRoughnessMetallic or *_ORM texture into _MaskMap while running a shader that is NOT MilkShaders/UERemap:
  MilkShaders/Lit-Template  91  e.g. weaponmodmaterials/acrop2 mat 'acrop2' -> acrop2_OcclusionRoughnessMetallic; weaponmodmaterials/ak_mag_akm_std mat 'AK_MAG_AKM_STD' -> AK_MAG_AKM_STD_OcclusionRoughnessMetallic
  HDRP/Lit                  14  e.g. charactermodmaterials/glove3 mat 'Glove3' -> T_Glove3_ORM; charactermodmaterials/glove5 -> T_Glove5_ORM
  shader PPtr unresolved    11  e.g. weaponmodmaterials/crc2u073 + crc2u073fde mat 'CRC9U028' -> CRC9U028_OcclusionRoughnessMetallic

Pixel probe of AK_MAG_AKM_STD_OcclusionRoughnessMetallic: R=0.623 (AO) G=0.796 (roughness) B=1.000 constant (metallic - correct for a steel AK mag) A=0.608 (min 136 max 172, a narrow band - not the 255 an ORM export normally writes).
Read as HDRP ordering that becomes metallic 0.62 / AO 0.80 / detail 1.0 / smoothness 0.61 - a semi-metal, semi-gloss mag instead of a rough steel one.

The authors clearly noticed something was off and papered over it with the remap floats rather than fixing the packing: AK_MAG_AKM_STD sets _Smoothness 0 and _SmoothnessRemapMax 0.886; MI_PMAG_556 sets _SmoothnessRemapMin 0 AND _SmoothnessRemapMax 0 (smoothness forced to zero) with _Metallic 1.0.
findings.names: acrop2_OcclusionRoughnessMetallic, AK_MAG_AKM_STD_OcclusionRoughnessMetallic, T_Glove3_ORM, T_Glove5_ORM, CRC9U028_OcclusionRoughnessMetallic, _SmoothnessRemapMax
findings.reskin: These 116 are the cheapest visual wins in the game: re-channel-swap the ORM into true HDRP MaskMap order (R<-B, G<-R, B=255, A<-1-G) and the surface becomes physically right without touching geometry or shaders. NEEDS A PROBE to be certain: dump the compiled MilkShaders/Lit-Template property block or Shader.Find it at runtime and read whether it declares a remap. Shaders are stripped in the player build, so this must be a runtime probe inside the game process (MelonLoader), not a bundle read.

findings.title: 21 MaskMaps are DXT1 - the alpha/smoothness channel is physically absent
findings.detail:
DXT1 (BC1) has no alpha. 21 textures whose name ends in MaskMap/ORM are stored as DXT1, so their A channel decodes to a hard 1.0 everywhere.
Proven on charactermodmaterials/mi_pmag_556: 'MI_PMAG_556_MaskMap' 2048x2048 DXT1 linear, bound to _MaskMap on material MI_PMAG_556 (HDRP/Lit, keyword _MASKMAP present). Decoded A = 1.000 with min=max=255. R=0.020, G=0.642, B=1.000 constant - the other three channels are correct HDRP packing, only smoothness is gone.
The material compensates by clamping: _SmoothnessRemapMin 0.0 AND _SmoothnessRemapMax 0.0, i.e. smoothness is force-zeroed and the mask's A is never actually used. _Metallic is set to 1.0 on the same material even though the mask's R says 0.02.
Same pattern in the ORM population: T_Glove2_ORM / T_Glove3_ORM / T_Glove5_ORM / T_Glove6_ORM / T_Glove7_ORM are all 1024x1024 DXT1, and AVS_bag_Roughness / AVS_bag_Metalness / Delta_MC_Roughness / Delta_MC_Metalness / Minimap_Black_Roughness / SATL_Black_Pack_Roughness are all DXT1 2048 single-purpose greyscale maps (3x the bytes they need).
findings.names: MI_PMAG_556_MaskMap, T_Glove2..7_ORM, AVS_bag_Roughness, AVS_bag_Metalness, Delta_MC_Roughness, Delta_MC_Metalness, _SmoothnessRemapMin, _SmoothnessRemapMax
findings.reskin: If you replace one of these with a proper DXT5 mask you must ALSO edit the material's _SmoothnessRemapMax back to 1.0, otherwise your gloss data is thrown away by the clamp and nothing changes on screen. This is the classic 'edited the right texture, saw no difference' trap for this game.

findings.title: 46% of the texture memory is duplicate-named copies; LitMask and MaskMap are the two highest-leverage/highest-risk shared names
findings.detail:
Addressables has no shared-asset group here: every bundle carries its own private copy of whatever it references. Grouping the 7,242 textures by m_Name gives 1,179 names appearing in 2 or more bundles, totalling 8.63 GB of the 18.73 GB GPU footprint in redundant copies.

Top shared names (count of distinct bundles, dims, redundant MB):
  LitMask                       x205  2048 DXT5 (120), 1024 (41), 512 (27), 2048x1024 (2), 256 (2)  ~1,088 MB
  MaskMap                       x274  512 DXT5 (137), 2048 (117), 1024 (20)                          ~91 MB
  BackPanel_Spiritus_MC_Normal  x27   1024/2048 DXT5                                                 ~35 MB
  Opscore_FAST_XP_Cover_Normal  x18   2048 DXT5                                                      ~91 MB
  Delta_MC_Normal               x17   2048 DXT5                                                      ~85 MB
  Airframe_Helmet_Normal        x17   2048 DXT5                                                      ~85 MB
  CryePantMask                  x20   1024 DXT5                                                      ~25 MB
  crye_g3_3                     x20   1024 DXT5                                                      ~25 MB
  ANPRC152_Normal               x20   512/2048 DXT5
  AVS_bag_Normal / _Roughness / _Metalness   x16 each  2048
  SATL_Black_Pack_Normal / _Roughness / _Metalness  x16 each  2048
  tShirtMask x15, TShirt_Black_Normal x15, Minimap_MC_Normal x15, Reticle03 x15 (1000x1000, weapons)

CRITICAL: LitMask and MaskMap are GENERIC names sitting in 205 and 274 unrelated bundles at four different resolutions. They are not one atlas - they are 205/274 different images that happen to share a name.

Worked example of the duplication, proven by opening both bundles:
  charactermodmaterials/mi_crye_pants_mcworn   -> cryeg2g3_MI_CRYE_Pants_MC_Normal 4096x4096 DXT5 (21.33 MB)
  charactermodmaterials/mi_crye_pants_aor1worn -> cryeg2g3_MI_CRYE_Pants_MC_Normal 4096x4096 DXT5 (21.33 MB, byte-identical name/size)
There are ~20 mi_crye_pants_* / mi_crye_ls_* slugs, each shipping its own copy of the same 4K normal.

findings.reskin: HIGHEST LEVERAGE: the normal and the mask are identical across every camo variant of a garment, so one authored normal has to be written into ~20 bundles to take effect everywhere - and conversely, editing only one bundle changes only one camo. Two textures called 'LitMask' in two bundles are different images, and the AOR1 pants ship a 1024/no-mip BaseMap while the MC pants ship a 2048/12-mip one under the SAME name.

findings.title: The camo seam: 217 character mods override ONLY _BaseColorMap with a loose texture; 23 swap a whole material
findings.detail:
Scanned the CharacterMod MonoBehaviour in all 1,165 charactermods_stripped bundles. Two mutually exclusive mechanisms, and the split is decisive:
  textureModifer=1 + baseColour PPtr set : 217 mods
  material PPtr set (no texture override): 23 mods
  neither (plain geometry mod)           : 927 mods
materialBaseColourReference is '_BaseColorMap' in ALL 217 cases - there is no second value in the game.

Mode A, texture override - PROVEN on charactermods_stripped/cryeg3camo10:
  GameObject 'CRYE G3 Camo 10'
  CharacterMod { textureModifer:1, modifyColour:1, materialIndex:0,
                 materialBaseColourReference:"_BaseColorMap",
                 baseColour -> Texture2D 'T_Shirt_CamoG_D' 2048x2048 DXT5 (in this same bundle),
                 Compatibility:"CRYEG3Shirt_Color", modSlot:11, characterSlot:0 }
  The bundle contains the texture and NO material. Normal and mask come from the shared garment material elsewhere; only base colour is swapped at runtime.

Mode B, material swap - PROVEN on charactermods_stripped/camoa:
  GameObject 'CamoA'
  Material 'M_PouchesCamoA' + Texture2D 'T_Pouches_CamoA_D' 32x32 + 'T_Pouches_N' 32x32 + 'M_PouchesCamoA_MaskMap' 1024x1024
  CharacterMod { textureModifer:0, materialIndex:3, material -> M_PouchesCamoA,
                 materialBaseColourReference:"", Compatibility:"Balaclava_Color" }

Override-texture resolutions: 1024x1024 x191, 2048x2048 x26. All DXT1 (format 10).
26 Compatibility groups total: HelmetNVG 29, BlackHawkFingerless_Color 25, OakleyPilot_Color 25, AssaultGloves_Color 24, M_Pacts_Color 24, OackleyHardKnuckle_Color 24 (sic), OakleyMPact_Color 24, BlackHawk_Color 23, Balaclava_Color 23, Patch 21, CRYEG3Shirt_Color 21, CRYEG3_Color 21, FAST XP HELM COVER 18, Helmet_Rear 12, Airframe_Cover 10, ArmourPlate 7, MechanicOriginal_Color 6, IHIPS_Cover 3, plus 8 singletons.

findings.reskin: This is the branch to start a camouflage project from. For Mode A you author ONE 1024 or 2048 DXT1 base-colour texture, drop it in the matching charactermods_stripped bundle, and the game does the rest - no material edit, no shader work, normal and mask untouched. Adding a NEW camo means cloning a camo bundle and giving it an unused AssetReferenceIndex/ModInfoIndex plus the right Compatibility string. For Mode B you must edit the whole material, and you inherit that mod's own normal+mask.

findings.title: Placeholder and dead art: 32x32 pouch camo, a 4x4 MaskMap, 299 orphan textures, and TextMeshPro font atlases inside character bundles
findings.detail:
32x32 CAMO - the entire Balaclava_Color / pouch camo set ships its base colour at 32x32 DXT5 while its own MaskMap is 1024x1024:
  T_Pouches_CamoA_D .. CamoI_D, T_Pouches_ColorA_D .. ColorI_D, all 32x32 DXT5; T_Pouches_N 32x32 DXT5 duplicated into 22 bundles.
  Pixel probe of T_Pouches_CamoA_D: R=0.433(55-151) G=0.383(52-135) B=0.285(31-106) - real variation, so it IS a camo pattern, just at 1/64th the linear resolution of the shirt camo (2048). Placeholder-tier art that shipped.
  Note also a copy-paste bug: charactermods_stripped/colorg contains a texture named 'T_Pouches_ColorH_D', and so does colorh. There is no ColorG texture.

4x4 STUB: 'M_Eye_MaskMap' 4x4 DXT1, bound to _MaskMap on material M_Eye (HDRP/Lit) in charactermodmaterials/m_eye. A 4x4 dummy standing in for a real mask; the material also sets _Smoothness 0 and _SmoothnessRemapMax 0.

CROSS-CONTAMINATION: the same M_Eye material binds _EmissiveColorMap -> 'T_Headgears_E' 256x256 DXT1 sRGB. A headgear emissive map wired into the eyeball material.

FONT ATLASES IN ART BUNDLES: 'amarurgt SDF Atlas' (charactermodmaterials/amarurgtsdf, Alpha8 1024) and 'LiberationSans SDF Atlas' (charactermods_stripped, Alpha8 1024) - TextMeshPro assets living in the character-gear families, with TextMeshPro/Distance Field and TextMeshPro/Mobile/Distance Field materials.

ORPHANS: 299 of 7,242 textures (0.33 GB) are present in a bundle that contains no material referencing them - all 299 in the *_stripped families (charactermods 226, weaponmods 73). Most are the camo swatches (bound at runtime, not statically - expected). But 3 copies of 'Vortex HD Gen 3 Reticle2' 4096x4096 DXT5 (16 MB each, mips=1) sit in vortex1-10x24eleanor, vortex1-10x24eleanorblkvariant and vortexrazorhdgeniii1-10x24 with nothing binding them.

DUPLICATE INSIDE ONE BUNDLE: weaponmodmaterials/cqb7_stock1 contains TWO separate Texture2D objects both named 'cqb7_stock_SpecularSmoothness' (2048 DXT5, sRGB) alongside cqb7_stock_Normal and cqb7_stock_MaskMap.

findings.title: 412 textures carrying linear data are flagged sRGB, including a whole camo family's opacity map
findings.detail:
m_ColorSpace: 0 = linear, 1 = sRGB. Classifying by name role:
  Color-role   : sRGB 2,027 / linear 10   (the 10 are XArrowDiffuse-2D-IES light cookies - correct as linear)
  Normal-role  : linear 2,177 / sRGB 5
  Mask/PBR-role: linear 1,991 / sRGB 407
412 textures total carry non-colour data but are marked sRGB, so the GPU applies an sRGB->linear curve to values that are already linear. Roughness/AO/opacity come out darker than authored.
Named offenders:
  CRYE_G3_MC_Opacity - sRGB, and it is duplicated across cryeg3aor3, cryeg3aor41, cryeg3cutaor4..8, cryeg3cutmcb, cryeg3mc and more (the whole Crye G3 camo family)
  PatchesL_T_Patches_MaskMap (charactermodmaterials/blackbeard) - sRGB
  cqb7_stock_SpecularSmoothness (weaponmodmaterials/cqb7_stock1) - sRGB
  head_mask (charactermodmaterials/m_head, 1024 DXT5) - sRGB, bound to _MaskMap on the GoreShader material M_Head
  Eyelashes_Opacity (charactermodmaterials/mi_eyelashes, 2048 DXT5) - sRGB, bound to _BaseColorMap on HDRP/Hair
  12 of the 205 'LitMask' copies and 12 'LitMask' at 512 are sRGB while the other 178 are linear - the SAME logical map inconsistently flagged between bundles.
findings.names: CRYE_G3_MC_Opacity, PatchesL_T_Patches_MaskMap, cqb7_stock_SpecularSmoothness, head_mask, Eyelashes_Opacity, LitMask, m_ColorSpace
findings.reskin: If you replace one of these and set the sRGB flag correctly, your texture will render BRIGHTER than the original even with identical pixels, and will no longer match its unedited siblings. Either keep the (wrong) flag to match, or fix the whole family at once. The LitMask sRGB/linear split across 205 bundles is the worst case - the same map renders differently on different items today.

findings.title: Mipmaps: 128 textures ship with no mip chain, including three 4096 reticles and the AOR1 Crye pants
findings.detail:
7,186 of 7,242 textures (99.2%) have m_StreamData set - mipmap streaming is on almost everywhere, so texture bytes live in the bundle's .resS blob and are demand-loaded per mip. 128 textures have m_MipCount == 1; 75 of those are >=256 px and 29 are >=1024 px.
Worst offenders (name, dims, family/slug):
  Vortex HD Gen 3 Reticle2   4096x4096 DXT5  weaponmods_stripped/vortex1-10x24eleanor, /vortex1-10x24eleanorblkvariant, /vortexrazorhdgeniii1-10x24
  Reticle4K                  2048x2048 DXT5  weaponmodmaterials/atacr18_rendertarget
  chevon@4x                  2048x2048 DXT5  weaponmodmaterials/acog_reticle
  hamr_reticle_illuminated   2048x2048 DXT5  weaponmodmaterials/bravo4_reticle1
  OKP7 Reticle               2048x2048 DXT5  weaponmodmaterials/okp7reticle, /okp7nvgreticle
  Patch_US_IR_BaseColor      2048x2048 DXT1  charactermodmaterials/mi_patch_3dma_us_ir, /mi_patch_us_bw1, /mi_patch_us_ir
  Patch_US_BW_BaseColor      2048x2048 DXT1  charactermodmaterials/mi_patch_us_bw
  cryeg2g3_MI_CRYE_Pants_MC_BaseMap 1024x1024 DXT1 charactermodmaterials/mi_crye_pants_aor1worn (m_MipCount=1, m_StreamData empty)
Reticles at mip 1 are defensible (they are sampled 1:1 through a scope). The IR/BW patches and the AOR1 pants base map are not - they will shimmer at distance, and the AOR1 pants are the only Crye variant in the family that does this while its MC sibling ships 2048 with 12 mips.
findings.names: Vortex HD Gen 3 Reticle2, Reticle4K, chevon@4x, hamr_reticle_illuminated, OKP7 Reticle, Patch_US_IR_BaseColor, Patch_US_BW_BaseColor, cryeg2g3_MI_CRYE_Pants_MC_BaseMap, m_MipCount, m_StreamData
findings.reskin: A replacement texture MUST carry the same m_MipCount and the same m_StreamData layout as the original, or the loader reads past the end of the .resS blob. This is the most likely cause of a corrupt/black texture after a hand-edited bundle swap. Rebuild through a Unity project rather than patching bytes when mip counts differ.

findings.title: The dual-world magazine trap, with the exact texture names on both sides
findings.detail:
Confirmed by opening all three bundles. The same physical Magpul PMAG exists three times with three unrelated texture sets:

1. charactermodmaterials/mi_mag_magpul_pmag_gen3_m3_556_30_blk (10.38 MB) - the mag in the CHEST RIG
   material MI_Mag_Magpul_PMAG_GEN3_M3_556_30_BLK, shader MilkShaders/Lit-Template
   _BaseColorMap Mag_Magpul_PMAG_GEN3_M3_556_30_BLK_BaseColor 2048 DXT1
   _NormalMap    Mag_Magpul_PMAG_GEN3_M3_556_30_Camo_DirectX_Normal 2048 DXT5
   _MaskMap      'MaskMap' 2048 DXT5   <- generic name, one of 274
2. charactermodmaterials/mi_pmag_556 (2.19 MB) - a SECOND character-side PMAG
   material MI_PMAG_556, shader HDRP/Lit
   _BaseColorMap PMAG_Black_BaseColor 1024 DXT1 | _NormalMap PMAG_Black_Normal 1024 DXT5 | _MaskMap MI_PMAG_556_MaskMap 2048 DXT1
3. charactermodmaterials/jpc_v2 - a THIRD PMAG baked into the plate carrier bundle
   material M4Pmag_sdr, shader HDRP/Lit
   _BaseColorMap m4Pmag_fbx_low_m4Pmag_sdr_BaseColor 512x512 DXT1 | _NormalMap m4Pmag_fbx_low_m4Pmag_sdr_Normal 256x256 DXT5
   (there is also a standalone charactermodmaterials/m4pmag_sdr and /mi_m4pmagfde)
The weapon side is a completely separate namespace: weaponmodmaterials/magazine holds Magazine_BaseColor 256x256 DXT1 / Magazine_Normal 512 DXT5 / Magazine_OcclusionRoughnessMetallic 256 DXT1, and weaponmodmaterials has 30+ other mag slugs (ak_mag_akm_std, emagblk, g28mag, hk_poly_magazine, magazine_20r, magazine_50, magazine_75rnd, l7awm_25_magazine_opaque_version / _translucent_version).

Note the resolution cliff: the JPC-carried PMAG is 512/256 while the standalone character PMAG is 2048 - the same object at 4-8x different texel density depending on which bundle drew it.

findings.reskin: Reskinning 'the PMAG' requires editing at least four bundles across two families, and each uses a different resolution, a different naming dialect and a different shader. Change one and the magazine on the chest still will not match the one in the rifle.

findings.title: Shader inventory and the texture-free material class (reticles, scope render targets, NVG)
findings.detail:
Shader assignments over all 2,601 materials (resolved by reading the Shader objects co-shipped in each bundle; 204 materials point at an external shader PPtr that is not in their bundle):
  HDRP/Lit 1,314 | MilkShaders/Lit-Template 439 | MilkShaders/UERemap 207 | <external> 204 | HDRP/Autodesk Interactive/AutodeskInteractive 116 | Shader Graphs/ClothWind 109 | HDRP/Unlit 80 | Ultimate Scope Shaders/HolographicSight 39 | Shader Graphs/RealisticNVG 2 39 | Shader Graphs/RealisticScopeEffect 18 | Shader Graphs/Reticle 8 | KriptoFX/FPS_Pack/Particles 6 | Shader Graphs/_NonDualRender RealisticScopeEffect 5 | HDRP/Hair 4 | HDRP/Decal 4 | GoreShader 2 | Shader Graphs/IR Laser 1 | Ultimate Scope Shaders/Scope 1 | KriptoFX/FPS_Pack/{Distortion, GlowAdditiveNoFade, AlphaBlendedAnim} 1 each | TextMeshPro/Distance Field 1 | TextMeshPro/Mobile/Distance Field 1.
Every bundle also ships a Hidden/*/FallbackError shader alongside (Hidden/HDRP/FallbackError + Hidden/Core/FallbackError for HDRP/Lit bundles, Hidden/Shader Graph/FallbackError for Shader Graph bundles) - that is the magenta you get when Shader.Find fails.

TEXTURE-FREE MATERIALS: weaponmodmaterials/acog_rendertarget and /razorhdg2e16_reticle contain a Material + Shader and ZERO Texture2D. acog_rendertarget runs Shader Graphs/RealisticScopeEffect with render queue 2000 and no bound texture at all - the scope image is generated at runtime from a RenderTexture (the one _SceneRender binding in the whole game). Reticle geometry is fed through _Reticle (40 bindings) and a bare 'Reticle' property (20 bindings).
weaponmodmaterials/muzzleparticles is a 20 KB bundle: KriptoFX/FPS_Pack/Particles + one 32x32 DXT5 texture called 'Particle', mips=1.

Unusual slots seen only once or twice: _MeatBaseMap / _MeatNormalMap (GoreShader, material M_Head, bound to meat_tile_AlbedoTransparency_1 and meat_tile_Normal, both 2048), _HeightMap (M_Eye -> T_EyeMidPlaneDisplacement, the only BC6H texture in the game), _OpacityMap (10), _DetailMap (6), _Emission (8), _OcclusionMap (27).

findings.reskin: HDRP/Lit materials mirror the base colour into BOTH _BaseColorMap and _MainTex - if you rebuild a material you must set both or half the pipeline reads the old texture. Scope reticles cannot be reskinned by editing textures; you must edit the Shader Graph or the RenderTexture path, which is a code mod, not an art mod.
